title_en: Aspiring Directors Program
description_en: Career transition programs are vital to supporting talent management across the public service. The Aspiring Directors Program (ADP) is a guided development activity for identified candidates to reflect on the competencies that are critical to the success of executives in the federal public service. Participants will explore the importance of self-awareness and personal reflection in becoming a better leader, and examine the leadership and self‑management skills needed to build teams and become an effective agent of change.
title_fr: Programme à l'intention des futurs directeurs
description_fr: Les programmes de transition de carrière sont essentiels pour soutenir la gestion des talents dans l'ensemble de la fonction publique. Le Programme à l'intention des futurs directeurs (PFD) s'agit d'une activité de développement guidée permettant aux candidats identifiés de réfléchir aux compétences qui sont essentielles au succès des cadres de la fonction publique fédérale. Les participants exploreront l'importance de la conscience de soi et de la réflexion personnelle pour devenir un meilleur leader, et examineront les compétences de leadership et d'autogestion nécessaires pour développer des équipes et devenir un agent du changement.
topics: Leadership/Leadership

title_en: Authority Delegation Training Program
description_en: To do their jobs effectively, public service managers are expected to have a solid understanding of their roles, responsibilities and accountabilities. The Authority Delegation Training Program (ADT) provides the essential information needed for managers and executives to successfully obtain and execute their delegated authorities in the areas of human resources, finance and procurement. Participants will learn about the core legislation, regulations, policies and guidelines that govern their roles and responsibilities within the federal public service.
title_fr: Programme de formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs
description_fr: Pour faire leur travail efficacement, les gestionnaires de la fonction publique doivent avoir une bonne compréhension de leurs rôles, de leurs responsabilités et de leurs obligations de rendre compte. Le programme de formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs (FDP) fournit l'information essentielle dont les cadres et les gestionnaires ont besoin pour qu'ils se voient déléguer des pouvoirs dans les domaines des ressources humaines, des finances et de l'approvisionnement et puissent bien les exercer. Les participants acquerront des connaissances sur les lois, les règlements, les politiques et les lignes directrices fondamentaux qui régissent leurs rôles et responsabilités dans la fonction publique fédérale.
topics: Leadership/Leadership

title_en: Grants and Contributions Series (COR2-PA1)
description_en:
The Grants and Contributions Learning Series is a collection of foundational courses that allow learners to better navigate through federal processes, stakeholder needs and policy requirements as they relate to transfer payment programs.

The series is primarily designed for program officers and program managers, as well as support staff and financial management personnel involved with the administration of transfer payments, but is open to all public servants interested in learning about government services.

Courses included in this series


1. Transfer Payment Basics (COR217) 
2. Authorities Related to Transfer Payments (COR218) 
3. Entering into a Funding Agreement (COR219)
4. Managing and Monitoring a Funding Agreement (COR220) 

Note: The courses should be taken in the order listed above.
title_fr: Série d'apprentissage sur les subventions et les contributions (COR2-PA1)
description_fr:
La série d'apprentissage sur les subventions et les contributions comprend des cours qui expliquent aux apprenant·es les fondements des processus fédéraux, des besoins des parties prenantes et des exigences politiques en ce qui concerne les programmes de paiements de transfert.

La série s'adresse principalement aux agent·es de programme et aux gestionnaires de programme, de même qu'au personnel de soutien et au personnel de gestion financière qui participent à l'administration des paiements de transfert, mais elle est offerte à tous les fonctionnaires qui souhaitent en apprendre davantage sur les services gouvernementaux.

Cours compris dans cette série


1. Notions de base sur les paiements de transfert (COR217) 
2. Autorisations liées aux paiements de transfert (COR218) 
3. Conclure une entente de financement (COR219)
4. Gestion et suivi d'une entente de financement (COR220)

Remarque : Les cours devraient être suivi selon l'ordre présenté ci-haut.

title_en: 2023 GC Data Stories (DDN3-V10)
description_en:
The GC Data Demo Library is a collection of data showcase videos highlighting innovations from across the GC data community for data conference 2023. They demonstrate the power of data to inform better policies, programs and operations. Cutting edge technologies that draw on the power of data, artificial intelligence, and machine learning help the public service innovate and remain relevant as an institution Canadians look to for excellent service, support, and leadership. As these technologies crunch numbers, summarize data, and process transactions, they provide new opportunities and avenues for public servants to focus on strategic and creative elements in ways never seen before. 

This video series explores how organizations across the federal government are using the power of data, artificial intelligence and machine learning to help the public service innovate and broaden their use moving forward.
title_fr: Récits des données du GC 2023 (DDN3-V10)
description_fr:
La bibliothèque de démos d’outils de données du GC est une collection de vidéos de projets de données mettant en évidence l’innovations de la communauté des données pour la Conférence sur les données du GC 2023. Elles démontrent le pouvoir des données pour informer de meilleures politiques, programmes et opérations. Les technologies de pointe qui exploitent la puissance des données, de l'intelligence artificielle et de l'apprentissage machine aident la fonction publique à innover et à demeurer l'institution de choix vers laquelle la population canadienne se tourne pour obtenir des services, du soutien et un leadership remarquables. Alors que ces technologies font des calculs, résument des données et traitent des transactions, elles offrent aux fonctionnaires des occasions et des moyens de se concentrer sur des éléments stratégiques et créatifs d'une manière jamais vue auparavant. 

Dans cette série, on explorera la façon dont les organisations du gouvernement fédéral exploitent la puissance des données, de l'intelligence artificielle et de l'apprentissage machine pour aider la fonction publique à innover et à se servir davantage de ces technologies à l'avenir.

title_en: Respecting Gender Identity in the Workplace (INC1-M01)
description_en:
Understanding and respecting gender diversity is essential for fostering inclusivity and a sense of belonging. This online self-paced micro-course begins with a short video, followed by reflection questions and resources that encourage learners to examine their assumptions, develop respectful practices, and navigate sensitive situations with empathy and care. Participants will learn strategies to create more supportive and respectful professional environments by building awareness of the nuances of gender identity and avoiding common mistakes.

Topics include:

- understanding the impacts of deadnaming and misgendering
- identifying inclusive behaviours
- responding to mistakes regarding gender identity
- demonstrating active allyship

title_en: Recognizing the Impacts of Systemic Anti-Black Racism in the Workplace (INC1-M02)
description_en:
Anti-Black racism remains a systemic issue in many workplaces. This online self-paced micro-course begins with a short video scenario depicting a Black public servant’s experience with systemic racism and its impacts, followed by reflection questions and resources. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of how systemic racism can affect career advancement and the mental and physical health of Black employees.

Topics include:

- understanding the barriers to career progression
- addressing discrimination and exclusion
- identifying the psychological impacts of systemic racism
- demonstrating active allyship

title_en: Anti-Black Racism in Canada: A Journey Through History (INC1-M04)
description_en:
Understanding the history of anti-Black racism is essential to recognizing the systemic barriers and racial inequalities that persist in Canadian society today. This online self-paced micro-course presents an interactive timeline of some key events in the history of anti-Black racism in Canada. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of both the historical roots and the ongoing impacts of anti-Black racism in Canada and the world today.

Topics include:

- exploring key historical events and examples of systemic anti-Black racism in Canada
- recognizing the lived experiences and the contributions of Black Canadians to Canadian society

Notes:

The timeline used in this course is adapted from the Fact Sheet: Key Historical Facts about Anti-Black Racism and Discrimination in Canada from the Department of Justice Canada.
title_fr: Racisme envers les personnes noires au Canada : un voyage à travers l’histoire (INC1-M04)
description_fr:
Il est essentiel, pour reconnaître les obstacles systémiques et les inégalités raciales qui persistent dans la société canadienne, de comprendre l’histoire du racisme envers les personnes noires. Ce microcours en ligne à rythme libre présente une chronologie interactive qui met en évidence des événements notables de l’histoire du racisme envers les personnes noires au Canada. Les participants comprendront mieux les racines historiques de ce racisme, mais aussi ses conséquences continues au Canada et ailleurs dans le monde.

Sujets traités :

- explorer des événements historiques notables et des exemples de racisme systémique envers les personnes noires au Canada;
- reconnaître les expériences et les contributions des personnes noires dans la société canadienne.

Remarques :

La chronologie présentée dans ce cours est une adaptation d’un produit du ministère de la Justice Canada intitulé Fiche d’information : Principaux faits historiques concernant le racisme et la discrimination envers les personnes noires au Canada.

title_en: Symposium on the Call to Action on Anti-Racism, Equity, and Inclusion in the Federal Public Service (INC1-V54)
description_en: This event recording of the first session of the Government of Canada Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Conference 2022 focuses on key areas to accelerate efforts, multiply promising practices and strengthen our commitment to the Call to Action on Anti-Racism, Equity, and Inclusion in the public service.

topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

title_en: Talent Management: Building the Future of the Public Service (INC1-V55)
description_en: This event recording of the second session of the Government of Canada Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Conference 2022 provides concrete examples of ways to improve diversity at all levels of the public service, including the development of meaningful performance management agreements, learning opportunities to combat unconscious bias, and the promotion of resources to foster personal growth, such as mentorship programs and sponsorship initiatives.
title_fr: Gestion des talents : bâtir la fonction publique de demain (INC1-V55)
description_fr: Cet enregistrement de la deuxième séance de la Conférence sur l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion du gouvernement du Canada de 2022 porte sur des façons concrètes d'améliorer la diversité à tous les niveaux de la fonction publique, comme par exemple, l'élaboration d'objectifs de rendement visant à promouvoir la diversité, les occasions d'apprentissage pour combattre les préjugés inconscients et la promotion des ressources pour favoriser la croissance personnelle, comme les programmes de mentorat et les initiatives de parrainage.
topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

title_en: Mental Health: Workplace Aggression, Bystander Intervention (INC1-V56)
description_en: This event recording of the third session of the Government of Canada Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Conference 2022 presents how workplace aggression has impacted members of equity-seeking groups and their mental health, and provides recommendations on ways to identify, address and prevent aggression in the workplace.
title_fr: Santé mentale : agressions en milieu de travail, intervention des témoins (INC1-V56)
description_fr: Cet enregistrement de la troisième séance de la Conférence sur l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion du gouvernement du Canada de 2022 porte sur les répercussions que les agressions en milieu de travail ont sur les membres de groupes en quête d'équité et sur leur santé mentale, en plus de fournir des recommandations sur les moyens de reconnaître, d'éliminer et de prévenir les agressions en milieu de travail.
topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

title_en: Creating a Culture of Integrity and Accountability in Upholding Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (INC1-V57)
description_en: This event recording of the fourth session of the Government of Canada Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Conference 2022 offers best practices for holding individuals and teams accountable in upholding the goals of equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) in order to create and maintain a safe and healthy work environment.
title_fr: Création d'une culture de l'intégrité et de la responsabilisation dans le respect de l'équité, de la diversité et de l'inclusion (INC1-V57)
description_fr: Cet enregistrement de la quatrième séance de la Conférence sur l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion du gouvernement du Canada de 2022 porte sur les pratiques exemplaires permettant de tenir les personnes et les équipes responsables du respect des objectifs d'équité, de diversité et d'inclusion en vue de créer et de maintenir un milieu de travail sain et sécuritaire.
topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

title_en: The Anti-Racism Framework for the Government of Canada (INC1-V58)
description_en: This event recording of the fifth session of the Government of Canada Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Conference 2022 introduces the anti-racism framework through a series of customized corporate and policy tools developed by the Federal Anti-Racism Secretariat of the Department of Canadian Heritage, as well as the Black-centric lens, developed by Employment and Social Development Canada.
title_fr: Cadre de lutte contre le racisme du gouvernement du Canada (INC1-V58)
description_fr: Cet enregistrement de la cinquième séance de la Conférence sur l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion du gouvernement du Canada de 2022 vise à présenter le cadre de lutte contre le racisme au moyen d'un ensemble d'outils organisationnels et stratégiques faits sur mesure par le Secrétariat fédéral de lutte contre le racisme du ministère du Patrimoine canadien, ainsi que de l'optique centrée sur les Noirs, un outil élaboré par Emploi et Développement social Canada.
topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

title_en: Navigating Faith, Spirituality and Religion in the Workplace (INC1-V59)
description_en: This event recording of the sixth session of the Government of Canada Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Conference 2022 features a panel discussion by individuals from various faith-based employee networks, sharing their experiences and ideas on how to overcome our misperceptions, implicit stereotypes and unconscious biases about religious minority groups in the workplace.
title_fr: Foi, spiritualité et religion au travail (INC1-V59)
description_fr: Cet enregistrement de la sixième séance de la Conférence sur l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion du gouvernement du Canada de 2022 consiste en une discussion réunissant des personnes de divers réseaux confessionnels de la fonction publique, qui parlent de leur expérience et expriment leurs idées sur la manière de surmonter les perceptions erronées, les stéréotypes implicites et les préjugés inconscients concernant les groupes religieux minoritaires en milieu de travail.
topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

title_en: Equity-Seeking Groups and 2021 Census Data (INC1-V60)
description_en: This event recording of the seventh and final session of the Government of Canada Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Conference 2022 explores the findings of Statistics Canada's February 2022 census data release related to citizenship and immigration, ethnocultural and religious composition of the population, and mobility and migration.
title_fr: Groupes en quête d'équité et données du recensement de 2021 (INC1-V60)
description_fr: Cet enregistrement de la septième et dernière séance de la Conférence sur l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion du gouvernement du Canada de 2022 porte sur les résultats du Recensement publiés par Statistique Canada en février 2022, en ce qui concerne la citoyenneté et l'immigration, la composition ethnoculturelle et religieuse de la population ainsi que la mobilité et la migration.
topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

title_en: The Current State of Artificial Intelligence Regulation (INC1-V61)
description_en: This video features Abdi Aidid, BA, JD, LLM, Canada School of Public Service Visiting Scholar and Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto Faculty of Law, Canada Research Chair in Artificial Intelligence and Access to Justice, who explores the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence (AI), with a focus on bias, transparency, and accountability, along with what public servants need to know to use AI responsibly while promoting fairness, protecting rights, and building public trust.

description_fr: Cette vidéo met en vedette Abdi Aidid, B.A., J.D., L.L.M., chercheur invité à l’École de la fonction publique du Canada, professeur adjoint à la Faculté de droit de l’Université de Toronto et titulaire d’une chaire de recherche du Canada sur l’intelligence artificielle et l’accès à la justice, qui examine l’évolution du paysage en matière d’intelligence artificielle (IA) en mettant l’accent sur les préjugés, la transparence et la responsabilité, ainsi que sur ce que les fonctionnaires doivent savoir pour utiliser l’IA de façon responsable tout en favorisant l’équité, en protégeant les droits et en renforçant la confiance du public.

title_en: Recognizing Microaggressions Towards Indigenous People (IRA1-M01)
description_en:
Subtle comments or behaviours, even when unintentional, can cause harm in the workplace by creating an environment where individuals feel excluded or undervalued. This micro-course introduces the concept of microaggressions towards Indigenous people and offers practical strategies to recognize and address them. Participants will deepen their understanding of microaggressions and learn how to help create a more inclusive and respectful work environment.

 

Topics include:

 

- defining microaggressions
- identifying common microaggressions experienced by Indigenous people
- acknowledging the impacts of microaggressions through a video case study
- responding respectfully when microaggressions occur

title_en: Introducing the Principles of Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit  (IRA1-M02)
description_en:
Recognizing and valuing Inuit knowledge systems is an essential part of public servants’ work to strengthen relationships with Inuit and support Canada’s strategic interests in the Arctic. This online self-paced micro-course introduces Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit (IQ), the traditional knowledge and wisdom of Inuit, and explores how its principles inform decision-making, governance, community life, and sustainable practices. Participants will deepen their understanding of Inuit worldviews and learn practical ways to reflect IQ principles in their work, supporting a more inclusive, culturally respectful, and effective public service.


Topics include: 

·recognizing the importance of IQ principles in fostering respectful relationships

·understanding the role of IQ principles in shaping Inuit culture and community well-being

·exploring the relationship between IQ principles and Western scientific knowledge in collaborative work

·connecting IQ principles and public service values
title_fr: Introduction aux principes de l’Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit (IRA1-M02)

title_en: Finding Health Equity for First Nations Children (IRA1-V43)
description_en: Everyone should have the opportunity to attain their full health potential. Avoidable, unfair or remediable differences in opportunity, whether they be social, economic, demographic or geographic, are a sign of an unacceptable inequity among groups of people. In its 2016 ruling, the Canadian Human Rights Tribunal found that First Nations children were being discriminated against as a result of the inequitable funding of child and family services. In this video, Dr. Cindy Blackstock, Ph.D., Executive Director of the First Nations Child and Family Caring Society of Canada, and Professor Sir Michael Marmot, Director of the International Institute for Society and Health, discuss the pursuit of equity for First Nations children in the context of Jordan's Principle and the Pan American Health Organization's recent report Just Societies: Health Equity and Dignified Lives.
title_fr: Inégalités en matière de santé chez les enfants des Premières Nations (IRA1-V43)
description_fr: Chacun devrait avoir la possibilité d’atteindre son plein potentiel en matière de santé. Les différences évitables, injustes ou remédiables entre les groupes de personnes sont des inégalités, que ces différences se reflètent sur les plans sociaux, économiques, démographiques ou géographiques. Dans sa décision de 2016, le Tribunal canadien des droits de la personne a conclu que les enfants des Premières Nations étaient victimes de discrimination en raison du financement inéquitable des services à l’enfance et à la famille. Dans cette vidéo, Cindy Blackstock, Ph. D., directrice générale de la Société de soutien à l’enfance et à la famille des Premières Nations du Canada, et Sir Michael Marmot, directeur de l’Institut international pour la société et la santé, abordent la poursuite de l’équité pour les enfants des Premières Nations dans le contexte du principe de Jordan et du récent rapport de l’Organisation panaméricaine de la santé intitulé Sociétés justes : équité en matière de santé et vies dignes (traduction libre de Just Societies: Health Equity and Dignified Lives).
topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

September 30 is now recognized as a federal statutory day of commemoration. The day provides an opportunity to reflect on the tragic history of residential schools and honour their Survivors by engaging in reconciliation activities within our communities. 
Guest speakers share their thoughts and insights on what those experiences mean for Indigenous Peoples in Canada and for us all as we continue the journey towards truth and reconciliation.

Des conférenciers font part de leurs réflexions et de leurs idées sur la signification de ces expériences pour les Autochtones au Canada et pour nous tous, alors que nous poursuivons notre parcours vers la vérité et la réconciliation.

title_en: The United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples explained (IRA1-V55)
description_en:
The United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples is the result of almost 25 years of collaboration between UN member states and Indigenous peoples from around the world. Indigenous leaders from Canada played a significant role in its development, including drafting and negotiating.
The United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act creates a lasting and action-oriented framework to advance federal implementation of the Declaration in consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples.
title_fr: Explication de la Déclaration des Nations Unies sur les droits des peuples autochtones (IRA1-V55)
description_fr:
La Déclaration des Nations Unies sur les droits des peuples autochtones est le résultat de près de 25 années de collaboration entre les États membres des Nations Unies et les peuples autochtones du monde entier. Les dirigeants autochtones au Canada ont joué un rôle important dans son élaboration, notamment dans sa rédaction et sa négociation.
La Loi sur la Déclaration des Nations Unies sur les droits des peuples autochtones crée un cadre durable et axé sur l'action pour faire progresser la mise en œuvre de la Déclaration par le gouvernement fédéral en consultation et en coopération avec les peuples autochtones.
topics: "Diversity, inclusion and Indigenous reconciliation/Diversité, inclusion et réconciliation avec les Autochtones"

title_en: Manager Development Program
description_en: For public service managers, managing people and performance includes ensuring that their employees are engaged and highly productive in serving the interests of Canadians. The Manager Development Program (MDP) is an important step in the learning path for new managers, offering valuable insights into the roles and accountabilities of managers in the federal public service, and the expectations placed upon them. Participants will develop the self-awareness and communication skills needed to succeed in their management role and thrive as a new team leader.
title_fr: Programme de perfectionnement des gestionnaires
description_fr: Pour les gestionnaires de la fonction publique, la gestion des personnes et du rendement consiste à assurer que leurs employés sont motivés et hautement productifs dans la prestation de services aux Canadiens. Le Programme de perfectionnement des gestionnaires (PPG) constitue une étape importante du parcours d'apprentissage des nouveaux gestionnaires, offrant un aperçu précieux des rôles et des responsabilités des gestionnaires dans la fonction publique fédérale, ainsi que des attentes à leur égard. Les participants développeront la conscience de soi et les compétences en communication nécessaires pour réussir dans leur rôle de gestionnaire et prospérer en tant que nouveau chef d'équipe.

The New Directors Program (NDP) provides an opportunity for new executives to better understand their role as a director within the Government of Canada and acquire the skills needed to effectively lead in today's work environment. Participants will explore a variety of leadership topics that will help them navigate through complex situations, be more resilient, adapt in times of change, and enhance their key leadership competencies as a new executive.

Le Programme à l'intention des nouveaux directeurs (PND) permet aux nouveaux cadres de mieux comprendre leur rôle de directeur au gouvernement du Canada et d'acquérir les compétences requises pour diriger efficacement dans l'environnement de travail d'aujourd'hui. Les participants exploreront différents sujets liés au leadership qui les aideront à traverser les situations difficiles, à accroître leur résilience, à s'adapter lors des périodes de changement et à améliorer leurs compétences clés en leadership en tant que nouveau cadre.

title_en: Supervisor Development Program: Virtual Edition
description_en: Becoming a supervisor is often the first major transition point in a public service career. The Supervisor Development Program: Virtual Edition (SDPv) offers a practical, hands-on approach to learning the core functions of the supervisory role and key concepts such as leadership, communication, delegation and engagement—all with an emphasis on people management. Participants will learn how to efficiently manage their priorities, time and teams, and how to apply their new supervisory skills in the workplace.
title_fr: Programme de perfectionnement des superviseurs : version virtuelle

Les participants apprendront à gérer efficacement leurs priorités, leurs ressources et leurs temps, et comment mettre en pratique leurs nouvelles aptitudes en supervision au lieu de travail.

·       contributing to risk identification and stakeholder analysis

title_en: Project Management Learning Path: Level 2 – Becoming a Practitioner (TRN3-PA2)
description_en:
Effective coordination and delivery of public sector projects require both technical knowledge and adaptive strategies. Level 2 of the Project Management Learning Path builds on foundational concepts to help learners apply a range of project methodologies to real-world initiatives. Participants will develop greater confidence in planning, stakeholder engagement, estimation, and tracking in a government context.


Topics include:

·       integrating predictive, agile, and hybrid methodologies

·       planning and managing scope, budget, schedule, and quality

·       analyzing and mitigating project risks

·       aligning stakeholder engagement with project objectives

·       interpreting data to support evidence-informed decisions

·       applying governance and reporting tools in public sector contexts


Note:

To explore Level 1 and Level 3, as well as related offerings, visit Project Management Learning Path.

title_en: Project Management Learning Path: Level 3 – Becoming a Project Expert (TRN3-PA3)
description_en:
Leading complex public sector initiatives demands deep expertise in governance, accountability, and strategic alignment. Level 3 of the Project Management Learning Path empowers experienced professionals to take full ownership of high-impact projects across departments or jurisdictions. Participants will strengthen their ability to lead teams, manage performance, and align project delivery with government-wide outcomes.

Topics include:

·       managing complex procurement relationships

·       leading teams through organizational change and uncertainty

·       evaluating performance metrics and reporting tools

·       applying agile principles in complex environments

·       exercising oversight across high-risk or cross-departmental projects

·       communicating strategic direction with executive stakeholders

Note:

To explore Level 1 and Level 2, as well as related offerings, visit Project Management Learning Path.

title_en: Exploring Energy in Canada Series: Understanding Regional Energy Realities (TRN5-V70)

description_fr: Dans cet enregistrement d’événement, des personnes représentant les régions du Nord, de l’Atlantique et des Prairies du Canada discutent de la façon de relever les défis énergétiques propres à leur région et de faire progresser leur avenir énergétique.
topics: Leadership/Leadership

title_en: Exploring Energy in Canada Series: Unpacking Energy Security (TRN5-V71)
description_en: This event recording explores Canada’s ability to ensure reliable and affordable energy by reviewing key historical events and illuminating the reality of energy poverty still faced by many Canadians.

topics: Leadership/Leadership

title_en: Outlining Canada's Energy Context (TRN5-V74)

description_fr: Cette vidéo porte sur le contexte énergétique canadien, et met en lumière la manière dont le pays produit et utilise de l’énergie, son rôle à titre d’exportateur majeur ainsi que les principaux défis et occasions qui façonneront son avenir énergétique.

description_en: This event recording explores the rise of artificial intelligence, including agentic AI, generative AI and artificial general intelligence, and offers perspectives on how international rules, competitive pressures, platform architectures, and geopolitical shifts are shaping the AI industry and Canada’s role in it.

title_en: Applying Climate Literacy Foundations (CHC101)
description_en:
Climate literacy for public servants means improving our ability to recognize how a changing climate affects our mandates and our ability to deliver on them. This online self-paced course provides the foundational knowledge needed to understand the science of climate change, with a focus on what a changing climate means for Canada and its citizens. Participants will learn how they can contribute to a climate-resilient, net-zero-emissions Canada and enhance their understanding of why climate literacy is an essential part of serving Canadians.
 
Topics include:
 
·      introducing the fundamentals of climate science
·      discussing climate impacts and solutions, including climate change mitigation and adaptation
·      understanding Indigenous knowledge, perspectives, and climate leadership
·      exploring governance, justice, and a shared responsibility for climate change
 
Notes:
 
After successfully completing this course, learners are invited to register for Contributing to a Net-Zero Canada (CHC102) and Adapting to a Changing Climate in Canada (CHC103) to learn more about climate change solutions and the role of public servants.
 
This course is delivered and maintained by Environment and Climate Change Canada.

title_en: Contributing to a Net-Zero Canada (CHC102)
description_en:
Canada has an ambitious yet achievable roadmap to reducing greenhouse gas emissions nationwide, joining over 120 countries in committing to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. This online self-paced course introduces Canada's Net-Zero Challenge, while exploring how public servants are critical to supporting this whole-of-society transition. Participants will explore the science underpinning Canada's net-zero emissions target and expand their knowledge of the policies designed to achieve it.
 
Topics include:
 
·      explaining why climate mitigation matters for Canadians and the federal public service
·      identifying energy systems and sources of Canadian greenhouse gas emissions
·      exploring climate mitigation policy through examples of practical solutions for different sectors
·      examining the role of public servants in contributing to the Net-Zero Challenge
 
Notes:
 
Applying Climate Literacy Foundations (CHC101) is a prerequisite for this course.
 
Learners are also invited to register for Adapting to a Changing Climate in Canada (CHC103) to learn more about the role of climate change adaptation in building a climate-resilient, net-zero Canada.
 
This course is delivered and maintained by Environment and Climate Change Canada.

title_en: Adapting to Climate Change in Canada (CHC103)
description_en: Canada is experiencing record-breaking climate events, with wide-ranging impacts on nature, people and the economy highlighting the urgent need to adapt to our changing climate. This online self-paced course explains the topics of climate change adaptation and resilience through practical examples that are relevant to public servants. Participants will learn why adapting to climate change is essential for building resilient communities and a strong economy while striving for net-zero emissions in Canada.   Topics include:   ·      explaining why climate change adaptation matters for Canadians and the federal public service ·      exploring the relationship between climate change mitigation and adaptation ·      reviewing case studies and other examples of adaptation in practice ·      examining the role of public servants in building climate resilience   Notes:   Applying Climate Literacy Foundations (CHC101) is a prerequisite for this course.   Learners are also invited to register for Contributing to a Net-Zero Canada (CHC102) to learn more about the role of climate change mitigation in building a climate-resilient, net-zero Canada.   This course is delivered and maintained by Environment and Climate Change Canada.
title_fr: S'adapter aux changements climatiques au Canada (CHC103)
description_fr: Il se produit au Canada des phénomènes météorologiques sans précédent, ayant d'importantes répercussions sur la nature, les gens et l'économie, ce qui fait ressortir le besoin urgent de nous adapter aux changements que subit notre climat. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre porte sur les thèmes de l'adaptation et de la résilience dans le contexte des changements climatiques, illustrés à l'aide d'exemples pratiques pertinents pour les fonctionnaires. Les participants apprendront pourquoi il est essentiel de nous adapter aux changements climatiques pour créer des collectivités résilientes et une économie forte, tout en visant la carboneutralité au Canada.   Sujets traités :   ·      expliquer pourquoi l'adaptation aux changements climatiques est importante pour la population canadienne et la fonction publique fédérale; ·      explorer la relation entre l'atténuation des changements climatiques et l'adaptation à ces changements; ·      examiner des études de cas et d'autres exemples d'adaptation mise en pratique; ·      examiner le rôle des fonctionnaires dans le renforcement de la résilience face au changement climatique.   Remarques :   Appliquer les principes de la lutte contre les changements climatiques (CHC101) est un préalable de ce cours. Les apprenants sont également invités à s'inscrire au cours Aider le Canada à atteindre la carboneutralité (CHC102) pour en apprendre davantage sur le rôle de l'atténuation des changements climatiques dans la création d'un Canada dans la création d'un Canada carboneutre et résilient face aux changements climatiques.   Ce cours est offert et maintenu par Environnement et Changement climatique Canada.

title_en: Introduction to Intellectual Property in the Public Sector (CHC104)
description_en:
Considering matters of intellectual property is an important part of the decision-making process for public servants at all levels. This online self-paced course imparts the essential knowledge needed to understand, identify and apply intellectual property (IP) considerations and best practices at work. Participants will learn about the different types of IP and their roles in managing or addressing IP in a way that optimizes outcomes and benefits for Canada and Canadians.

Topics include:

•	defining what IP is and why it is important

•	distinguishing between formal and informal IP rights

•	identifying IP considerations unique to the public service

•	learning about confidentiality and disclosure

•	reviewing commercialization and licensing

Notes:

This course is delivered and maintained by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.

title_en: Fundamentals of Job Classification (CHC105)
description_en:
Understanding the legislative and policy framework related to workplace organization and classification is an essential first step to providing guidance, and making informed decisions about classification. This online self-paced course provides an overview of the organization and classification framework of the core public administration of the Government of Canada, and explains how it fits into the Policy on People Management. Participants will explore concepts that will enable them to fully understand the inner workings of the federal Classification Program.

Topics include:

•	examining the occupational group structure

•	identifying the documents required in the analysis process

•	introducing the classification decision process and its potential impacts

•	identifying stakeholders in organization and classification and their roles and responsibilities

•	presenting the legislative and governance foundations of the Classification Program, and the powers emanating therefrom

Notes:

This course fulfills the first part of the mandatory learning program for human resources advisors seeking accreditation in organization and classification. The program includes CHC106, CHC107 and CHC108 (under development), for which CHC105 is a prerequisite.
This course is delivered and maintained by Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat.

title_en: Performing Classifications Actions (CHC106)
description_en:
The Directive on Classification provides flexibility to organizations by enabling individuals who are not accredited and sub-delegated in classification to process and approve classification actions. This online self-paced course explores classification actions that are common to organizational design and classification professionals, and provides the foundational knowledge needed to perform these actions. Participants will be guided through several practical scenarios, including how to create, change and delete positions within their organization.
 
Topics include:
 
·      creating a position using a standardized job description
·      changing the reporting relationship of a position
·      changing the title of a position
·      deleting a position
 
Notes:
 
This course is mandatory and must be taken before individuals can exercise Section 4.4 of the Directive on Classification. Persons trained in organizational design and classification must be authorized to exercise these responsibilities through a formal mechanism established by their organization.
 
This course is also part of the mandatory learning curriculum for human resources advisors seeking an accreditation in organizational design and classification.

This course is delivered and maintained by Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat.

This online self-paced course explains the requirements of the Policy on Communications and Federal Identity, as well as the role of the Copyright Media Clearance Program in detecting and tracking emerging media trends and issues. Participants will learn about their specific roles and responsibilities towards media monitoring, how to comply with copyright rules, and how to access online news, magazines, newswires, transcripts and more.

 

Topics include:

 

·         reinforcing the importance of media monitoring

·         reviewing the intricacies of journalism and copyright

·         explaining the role of the Copyright Media Clearance Program

This course is delivered and maintained by Public Services and Procurement Canada.

title_en: Advanced Green Procurement (CHC111)
description_en:
Procurement practitioners play a crucial role in contributing to and delivering on Canada’s Greening Government Strategy and the wider Federal Sustainable Development Strategy. This course bridges theory into practice by examining the role of procurement officers and their ability to develop strategic approaches. This course incorporates green and other complex socio-economic considerations into government contracts supporting Program Delivery to Canadians.


Topics include:


·         Understanding the Circular Economy and its elements

·         The roles of key stakeholders and their responsibilities in greening initiatives

·         Sourcing greener goods, services, and suppliers

·         Identifying risks and opportunities associated with Green Procurement

·         Applying Green Procurement strategies to the acquisition of goods and services

Developing evaluation criteria for Green Procurement
title_fr: Cours avancé sur les achats écologiques (CHC111)
description_fr:
Les spécialistes de l’approvisionnement jouent un rôle crucial en contribuant au succès de la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie du Canada pour un gouvernement vert et de la Stratégie fédérale de développement durable. Ce cours fait le lien entre la théorie et la pratique en examinant le rôle des agents et agentes d’approvisionnement et leur capacité d’élaborer des approches stratégiques. Ce cours permet d’intégrer des considérations écologiques et des considérations socioéconomiques complexes dans les contrats gouvernementaux qui appuient la prestation des programmes pour la population canadienne.


Sujets abordés


·         La compréhension de l’économie circulaire et de ses éléments

·         Les rôles des principales parties prenantes et leurs responsabilités dans les initiatives d’écologisation

·         L’approvisionnement en biens, services et fournisseurs plus écologiques

·         La détermination des opportunités et des risques liés aux achats écologiques

·         L’utilisation de stratégies d’achats écologiques dans l’acquisition de biens et de services

·         L’élaboration de critères d’évaluation pour les achats écologiques

title_en: Halting and Reversing Biodiversity Loss in Canada (CHC112)
description_en:
Nature is an intrinsic part of Canada's national identity, yet its biodiversity is declining faster than at any time in history. This online self-paced course explores the relevance of nature for Canadians and the impacts of biodiversity loss and its two-way relationship with climate change. Participants will learn about the foundations of biodiversity, the contribution of nature to the Canadian identity, and practical strategies for integrating nature and biodiversity into the decision-making process.

 

Topics include:

 

·         exploring the relevance of nature and biodiversity for Canadians

·         highlighting solutions to biodiversity loss and the two-way relationship between climate change and biodiversity

·         integrating Indigenous knowledge, perspectives and leadership into nature stewardship

·         exploring governance, justice and our shared responsibility towards nature

·         making data-driven decisions and engaging in research-based transformative actions for the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity

 

Notes:

 

After successfully completing this course, learners are invited to register for Applying Climate Literacy Foundations (CHC101), Contributing to a Net-Zero Canada (CHC102), and Adapting to a Changing Climate in Canada (CHC103) to learn more about how public servants can integrate considerations about climate change and nature into their decision-making.

 

This course is delivered and maintained by Environment and Climate Change Canada.

title_en: Advancing the United Nations' 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development (CHC113)
description_en:
The United Nations' 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development serves as a global call to action to address today's most pressing social, economic, and environmental challenges. This online self-paced course presents an overview of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and its 17 sustainable development goals. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of Canada’s commitment to the 2030 Agenda and learn how to integrate those goals into government policies, programs and decision-making.

title_fr: Faire avancer le Programme de développement durable à l’horizon 2030 des Nations Unies (CHC113)
description_fr:
Le Programme de développement durable à l’horizon 2030 des Nations Unies sert d’appel à l’action mondial pour s’attaquer aux enjeux les plus urgents sur le plan social, économique et environnemental. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente un aperçu du Programme de développement durable à l’horizon 2030 et de ses 17 objectifs en matière de développement durable. Les participants comprendront mieux l’engagement du Canada envers ce programme et apprendront à intégrer ses objectifs dans les politiques, les programmes et la prise de décisions du gouvernement.

Sujets traités :

 

- expliquer le Programme de développement durable à l’horizon 2030 et ses objectifs;
- comprendre l’engagement du Canada à faire avancer ce programme;
- intégrer les objectifs de développement durable aux politiques, aux programmes et à la prise de décisions du gouvernement.

 

Remarques :

Ce cours est conçu par Emploi et Développement social Canada.

title_en: Communicating Risk Effectively (CHC114)
description_en:
Risk communication is the exchange of information between government, experts, interest holders and the community about a risk with the goal of empowering individuals to engage in risk prevention or harm reduction. This online self-paced course presents the foundational knowledge and practical skills needed to communicate risks effectively. Participants will explore the key aspects of risk communication through theory, tools, and real-life examples, and will apply their newfound knowledge through a learning scenario that references the Toolkit for Risk Communicators.

 

Topics include:

 

- reviewing the foundational concepts of risk communication
- identifying best practices for communicating uncertainty
- managing misinformation and disinformation
- creating inclusive communication strategies
- understanding ethics in risk communication

 

Notes:

 

This course is recommended for communicators at all levels who are seeking to understand or enhance their knowledge of risk communication principles and processes.

title_en: Introduction to Ethical Procurement (CHC118)
description_en:
The Government of Canada aims to use its purchasing power to promote ethical business practices in Canada and abroad. This online self-paced course introduces the concept of ethical procurement and provides an overview of the annual reporting obligations for government institutions under the Fighting Against Forced Labour and Child Labour in Supply Chains Act. Participants will explore key tools, requirements, and resources available in the federal government to support ethical procurement practices.

 

Topics include:

·       understanding ethical procurement in the Government of Canada

·       identifying the risks of human trafficking, forced labour, and child labour in federal supply chains

·       examining Canadian legislation and international standards on human rights

·       applying requirements for ethical procurement

 

Notes:

 

This course helps procurement professionals build a general understanding of human rights risks in federal supply chains. Since it focuses on the federal procurement context, it does not cover all legal definitions or obligations. Participants should therefore continue to consult departmental authorities to ensure compliance with relevant laws, regulations, policies, and contracts.

 

This course is intended for Government of Canada procurement professionals and other employees interested in learning about ethical procurement.

title_en: Responding to Vendor Performance Management Surveys in SAP Ariba (CHC121)
description_en:
The Vendor Performance Management program from Public Services and Procurement Canada is designed to strengthen the procurement process by capturing feedback on vendor performance. This online self-paced course for technical authorities explains how to complete a vendor performance management scorecard during an evaluation cycle by responding to surveys in the SAP Ariba online procurement system. Participants will learn how to navigate in SAP Ariba to complete and submit vendor performance management scorecards in support of timely vendor performance evaluations.

Topics include:

•         accessing an open survey from an email invitation

•         completing the scorecard attached to each survey

•         submitting survey results to the buyer

•         accessing projects and completed surveys related to a project

Notes:

This course is designed and maintained by Public Services and Procurement Canada.
title_fr: Répondre aux sondages sur la gestion du rendement des fournisseurs dans SAP Ariba (CHC121)
description_fr:
Le programme de gestion du rendement des fournisseurs de Services publics et Approvisionnement Canada est conçu pour renforcer le processus d’approvisionnement en recueillant la rétroaction sur le rendement des fournisseurs. Dans ce cours en ligne à rythme libre, les autorités techniques apprendront comment remplir une carte d’évaluation de la gestion du rendement des fournisseurs au cours d’un cycle d’évaluation, en répondant à des sondages dans le système d’approvisionnement en ligne SAP Ariba. Les participants apprendront aussi à naviguer dans SAP Ariba pour remplir et soumettre les cartes d’évaluation de la gestion du rendement des fournisseurs, à l’appui de la réalisation des évaluations en temps opportun.

 

Sujets traités :

 

•         accéder à un sondage ouvert à partir d’une invitation par courriel

•         remplir la carte d’évaluation jointe à chaque sondage

•         soumettre les résultats du sondage à l’acheteur

•         accéder aux projets et aux sondages déjà remplis pour chaque projet

 

Remarque :

 

Ce cours est conçu et tenu à jour par Services publics et Approvisionnement Canada.

Ce parcours combine des compétences numériques de base, des méthodes de travail agiles, une conception centrée sur l'humain, la gestion de projet et la gestion des risques, le tout ancré dans les normes numériques du gouvernement du Canada. Il est idéal pour ceux qui recherchent des compétences pratiques et un état d'esprit propice à l'innovation, à la collaboration et à l'amélioration continue dans la prestation des services publics.

title_en: Demystifying Your Pay Stub (COR105)
description_en:
Understanding the terminology, payments and deductions on federal government pay stubs can sometimes be confusing. This online self-paced course helps to decipher the information displayed on pay stubs made available through Phoenix, the Compensation Web Applications (CWA), and the newest web application, MyGCPay. Participants will learn to interpret common pay factors, resolve issues, and access centralized pay information.

Topics include:

- understanding the information on a Compensation Web Applications (CWA) pay stub
- understanding the information on a Phoenix pay stub
- finding centralized pay information using the MyGCPay application

title_en: Managing Unsatisfactory Performance (COR107)
description_en:
Managers need to be equipped to confidently deal with unsatisfactory employee performance within their teams. This course examines a range of tools, skills and techniques designed to help managers carry out positive employee performance management, including practical options for addressing culpable and non-culpable behaviours. ·       applying the performance management decision-making process

title_en: Performance Management for the Government of Canada (COR109)
description_en:
Creating and sustaining a culture of high performance in the Government of Canada is key to ensuring the delivery of high-quality programs and services to Canadians. This online self-paced course, which is mandatory for managers and supervisors with performance management responsibilities, provides the information they need to fulfill their various roles and implement performance management principles and practices. In preparation for an online certification test, participants will study the basic concepts of performance management and related time-specific requirements, identify different types of behaviour, and learn how to apply best practices and effective techniques through useful, real-life exercises.

title_en: Labour Relations in the Federal Public Sector (COR110)
description_en:
It is essential that managers and human resources specialists in the federal public sector be well equipped to deal with labour relations matters. This online self-paced course presents the fundamentals of labour relations in the federal public sector, including rules and best practices to follow when managing employees. Participants will study the policy and legislative frameworks that govern labour relations and gain a better understanding of the rights, obligations, roles and responsibilities of management, employees and bargaining agents.
 
Topics include:
 
- interpreting and applying collective agreements
- distinguishing between disciplinary and non-disciplinary matters
- handling unsatisfactory performance, probation and medical incapacity
- understanding grievances and dispute resolution
 
Notes:
 
This course represents the common core learning in labour relations for managers and human resources specialists.

title_en: Basics of Staffing in the Public Service (COR111)
description_en:
When looking to add new skills and competencies to their team, managers must first plan their staffing criteria and select the right staffing options. This online self-paced course reviews the legislative framework that governs staffing in the federal public service and explores staffing requirements, merit criteria, staffing options and other factors influencing the choice of staffing process. Participants will learn about the vision of staffing in the public service, the delegation of staffing authorities, how appointment processes are conducted, the key players involved, and how staffing interacts with the other human resources disciplines. 

Topics include: 

· staffing within the legislative framework 

· staffing strategically according to predetermined goals 

· establishing staffing and merit criteria 

· planning and executing a staffing process 

· assessing the staffing types, options and factors influencing the choice of staffing process 

Notes: 

This course is intended for human resources advisors, managers and anyone else who is interested in learning about staffing in the public service. It consists of two content modules followed by an exam, which serves to assess and validate the knowledge acquired. Participants must finish all three modules to complete this course. 

This course has been redesigned to amalgamate the former H200-1,
H200-2 and H200-3 courses into a single learning activity and registration process. 

This course makes frequent reference to the terms and conditions listed in
the Public Service Employment Act (PSEA) since most federal public service
organizations are subject to this Act.

description_en:
The Public Service Employment Act makes managers responsible and accountable for their staffing. This online self-paced course provides managers with the knowledge they need to establish merit criteria, explore the staffing options available to them, and manage the candidate assessment process. Participants will learn how to choose the most effective resourcing strategies and options based on applicable legislation and policies, and about making sound decisions throughout the hiring process.

 

Topics include:

title_en: Collective Agreements and Terms and Conditions of Employment for Managers (COR114)
description_en:
It is essential that managers in the federal public sector understand their roles and responsibilities towards respecting collective agreements and terms and conditions of employment. This course provides managers with a comprehensive overview of collective agreements and the terms and conditions of employment, including the information they need to correctly respond to questions about employee rights and obligations in the workplace. Participants will gain a better understanding of the day-to-day application of collective agreements and their impact on human resources management decisions.

Topics include:

- Outlining the structure and content of collective agreements
- Applying the rules and principles for interpreting collective agreements
- Adapting the application of terms and conditions of employment to support work-life balance
- Clarifying the scope of managers' delegated authority in applying the provisions of collective agreements

Notes:

It is strongly recommended that learners complete Labour Relations in the Federal Public Sector (COR110) before registering for this course, which represents the common core learning in labour relations for managers and human resources specialists.

description_en:
HR practitioners play a crucial role in allowing an organization to provide strategic guidance and make informed decisions on matters of human resourcing. This online self-paced course examines the strategic role of senior HR practitioners, the different HR perspectives, and the forward-thinking skills needed to provide strategic HR guidance. Participants will learn about the analytics tools available to them and how to conduct in-depth analyses, propose risk-informed solutions, and address complex and strategic HR challenges.

title_en: Inclusive Hiring Practices for a Diverse Workforce (COR120)
description_en:
As Canada's largest employer, the Public Service of Canada has a responsibility to reflect the diversity of the Canadian people and to be representative of the people it serves. This online self-paced course presents best practices and staffing strategies for conducting an inclusive and bias-free hiring process. Participants will learn about the importance of a diverse workforce and the impact that unconscious bias and other barriers can have when recruiting new talent.

• recognizing the importance of diversity and inclusion in the federal public service
• understanding the impact of unconscious bias in the hiring process
• acknowledging potential barriers in order to attenuate or eliminate them
• identifying tools and strategies for conducting fair, inclusive and accessible staffing processes
This course is expected to launch in the late fall of 2021.

Related courses:

• Understanding Unconscious Bias (W005)
• Overcoming Your Own Unconscious Biases (W006)
• Overcoming Unconscious Bias in the Workplace (W007)
title_fr: Pratiques d'embauche inclusives pour un effectif diversifié (COR120)
description_fr:
À titre de plus grand employeur au Canada, la fonction publique du Canada a la responsabilité de refléter la diversité de la population canadienne et d'être représentative des personnes qu'elle sert. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente les pratiques et les stratégies exemplaires de dotation pour mener un processus d'embauche inclusif et sans biais. Les participants apprendront sur l'importance d'un effectif diversifié et l'impact que les biais et préjugés inconscients et autres obstacles peuvent avoir lors du recrutement de personnes de talent.

Sujets traités :

•	reconnaître l'importance de la diversité et de l'inclusion dans la fonction publique fédérale;
•	comprendre l'impact des biais et préjugés inconscients au cours du processus d'embauche;
•	reconnaître les obstacles potentiels afin de les atténuer ou de les éliminer;
•	présenter des outils et des stratégies pour mener des processus de dotation équitables, inclusifs et accessibles.

Remarques :

Ce cours est destiné aux gestionnaires subdélégués, aux spécialistes en ressources humaines et aux autres personnes participant à un processus d'embauche.

Cours connexes :

• Compréhension des préjugés inconscients (W005)
• Surmonter vos propres préjugés inconscients (W006)
• Dépasser les préjugés inconscients au travail (W007)

title_en: The 5 Essential Steps to Integrated Business and Human Resources Planning (COR122)
description_en:
Effective staffing requires a plan that involves all of the stakeholders who work to respond to the human resources needs of an organization. This online self-paced course explores integrated business and human resources planning (IBHRP) and introduces a five-step human resources planning model designed to support it. Participants will review the roles of the various stakeholders involved in resource utilization and examine the relationship between planning and the different human resource disciplines.
 
Topics include:
 
- identifying the inputs and outputs of IBHRP
- defining the roles of different stakeholders in the planning processes
- outlining the steps in the IBHRP process
 
Notes:
 
This course is intended for human resources advisors; however, registration remains open to all learners.
title_fr: Les 5 étapes essentielles de la planification intégrée et des ressources humaines (COR122)
description_fr:
Pour prendre des mesures de dotation efficaces, il faut établir un plan qui fait appel à tous les intervenants qui ont pour mission de répondre aux besoins en matière de ressources humaines d'une organisation. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre explore la planification intégrée des activités et des ressources humaines (PIARH) et présente un modèle de planification des ressources humaines en cinq étapes conçu pour l'appuyer. Les participants passeront en revue les rôles des divers intervenants concernés par l'utilisation des ressources et ils examineront la relation entre la planification et les différentes disciplines des ressources humaines.
 
Sujets traités :
 
- connaître les intrants et les extrants de la PIARH;
- définir les rôles des différents intervenants dans le cadre des processus de planification;
- décrire les étapes du processus de PIARH.
 
Remarques :
 
Ce cours est destiné aux conseillers en ressources humaines, mais tous les apprenants peuvent s'y inscrire.

title_en: Understanding Workforce Adjustment (COR123)
description_en:
Workforce adjustment is a situation wherein the services of an indeterminate employee are no longer required beyond a specific date. This online self-paced course provides managers and human resources specialists with an overview of the core public administration's workforce adjustment process and explains how to manage and mitigate its impacts effectively. Participants will learn how to interpret and apply the provisions in the National Joint Council's Work Force Adjustment Directive and the workforce adjustment appendices to some Government of Canada collective agreements for the core public administration.

Topics include:

- understanding the workforce adjustment appendices and the National Joint Council's Work Force Adjustment Directive
- describing the roles, responsibilities, rights and obligations of key stakeholders
- uncovering the key elements of the workforce adjustment process
- introducing the process of selecting employees for retention or layoff
- outlining career transition options for executives

Notes:

It is recommended that participants read the National Joint Council's Work Force Adjustment Directive and the workforce adjustment appendices to collective agreements for the core public administration prior to taking this course.

title_en: Collective Agreements and Terms and Conditions of Employment for Human Resources Specialists (COR124)
description_en:
It is essential that human resources professionals in the federal public sector understand their roles and responsibilities towards respecting collective agreements and terms and conditions of employment. This course provides labour relations advisors and human resources specialists with a comprehensive
overview of collective agreements and the terms and conditions of employment, including the information they need to correctly respond to questions about employee rights and obligations in the workplace. Participants will gain a better understanding of the day-to-day application of collective agreements and their impact on human resources management decisions. 

Topics include: 

· outlining the structure and content of collective agreements 

· understanding the rules and principles for interpreting collective agreements 

· applying flexibility in terms and conditions of employment to support work-life balance 

· clarifying the scope of managers' delegated authority in applying the provisions of collective agreements 

Notes: 

This course consists of three 2.5-hour virtual sessions offered during the same week. Participants will be informed of the date and time of each virtual session once they are registered. 

It is strongly recommended that learners complete Labour Relations in the Federal Public Sector (COR110) before registering to this course, which represents the common core learning in labour relations for managers and human resources specialists.

title_en: Becoming a Strategic HR Practitioner, Part 2: From Theory to Practice (COR128)
description_en:
HR practitioners play a crucial role in allowing an organization to provide strategic guidance and make informed decisions on matters of human resourcing. This course bridges theory into practice by examining the strategic role of senior HR practitioners and their ability to provide informed guidance on strategic HR decisions. By integrating analytical tools and developing forward-thinking skills, participants will enhance their ability to conduct comprehensive analyses and design risk-sensitive solutions for their HR management teams.

 

Topics include:

 

- exploring the nuances of strategic perspectives and strategic behaviour
- understanding the pivotal strategic role played by HR practitioners
- navigating the intricate steps of conducting exhaustive strategic analyses
- crafting solutions rooted in meticulous risk evaluation
- mastering an array of tools that facilitate the adoption of strategic HR perspectives

 

Notes:

 

This course is part 2 of a two-part course suite, which begins with the prerequisite Becoming a Strategic HR Practitioner: Fundamentals (COR118) (online self paced), followed by Becoming a Strategic HR Practitioner: From Theory to Practice (COR128) (in person or virtual instructor-led).

title_en: Staffing for HR Specialists, Part 1: Understanding (COR129)
description_en:
To meet the evolving needs of hiring managers, human resources (HR) specialists must navigate through complex staffing actions, work closely with clients, and understand the distinction between requirements and considerations when making recommendations. This course (Part 1 of 3) introduces the foundational elements of the legislative and policy frameworks that underpin staffing in the public service. Participants will receive practical advice from experts to develop a greater understanding of their role as an HR specialist, and reflect on how to work collaboratively with clients and partners.

Topics include:

- defining the staffing context in the public service, including the legislative and policy frameworks
- analyzing the nature and context of staffing needs
- evaluating and recommending staffing options based on impact and business value
- gathering information, receiving feedback, and drafting relevant options
- identifying equity, diversity and inclusion considerations as they relate to staffing actions

Notes:

Before registering for this course, participants must first complete the following prerequisite courses:


1. Basics of Staffing in the Public Service (COR111)
2. Inclusive Hiring Practices for a Diverse Workforce (COR120)

   \

To receive a certificate of completion for COR129, participants must attend the two virtual classroom sessions over the course of three weeks and complete the online self-paced modules before the second virtual instructor-led session:


1. Virtual instructor-led session 1 (week 1, 2.5 hours)
2. Self-paced modules 1 to 4 (approximately 10 hours of work)
3. Virtual instructor-led session 2 (week 3, 2.5 hours)

title_en: Staffing for Managers, Part 2: Practical Application (COR132)
description_en:
The Public Service Employment Act makes managers responsible and accountable for their staffing. This course presents a practical framework for exercising delegated staffing authority as a manager. Participants will be taken through various scenarios to reflect and exchange on the considerations to be taken into account during the staffing process and the implications of each.

Topics include:

·        establishing effective merit criteria

·        developing a candidate assessment strategy

·        identifying prejudices and barriers, and ways of eliminating or mitigating them

Notes:

This course is part 2 of a two-part course suite, which begins with the prerequisite Staffing for Managers, Part 1: Building on the Basics (COR112) (online self-paced), followed by Staffing for Managers, Part 2: Practical Application (COR132) (virtual instructor-led).
title_fr: Dotation à l'intention des gestionnaires, partie 2 : Application des principes de base (COR132)
description_fr:
En vertu de la Loi sur l'emploi dans la fonction publique, la responsabilité de la dotation et l'obligation d'en rendre compte incombent aux gestionnaires. Ce cours porte sur un cadre pratique pour exercer des pouvoirs délégués en matière de dotation en tant que gestionnaire. Les participants étudieront diverses mises en situation qui les amèneront à réfléchir aux considérations à prendre en compte tout au long du processus de dotation et aux implications de chacune d'elles, ainsi qu'à échanger à ce sujet.

Sujets traités :

·        établir des critères de mérite efficaces;

·        élaborer une stratégie d'évaluation des candidatures;

·        identifier les biais et les obstacles, et déterminer des moyens de les éliminer ou de les atténuer.

Remarques :

Ce cours est la deuxième partie d'un ensemble de deux cours. Les participants doivent d'abord suivre le cours préalable Dotation à l'intention des gestionnaires, partie 1 : Consolider les principes de base (COR112) (en ligne à rythme libre), puis le cours Dotation à l'intention des gestionnaires, partie 2 : Application des principes de base (COR132) (cours en classe virtuelle dirigé par un enseignant).

title_en: Introduction to Organization and Classification (COR133)
description_en:
As per the Directive on Classification, training is required to ensure that classification decisions are well managed and are made in the public interest. This online self-paced course is the first step in the mandatory training and accreditation of public servants working and specializing in classification. Participants will learn about the concepts of classification and organizational design, the roles and responsibilities of the main players, the scope of classification action requests, and the impacts of classification decisions and changes to organizational structure and job descriptions.

Topics include:

·       introducing classification ·       exploring organizational design ·       evaluating job descriptions ·       understanding the impacts of classification decisions

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.

This course is mandatory training and must be taken by all managers who authorize organizational structures or organizational charts, approve job descriptions, and/or authorize classification action requests. All new managers who only have delegated classification responsibilities must complete this training within the first 6 months of assuming their new duties in accordance with the Directive on Mandatory Training.

This course is also mandatory for organization and classification trainees who wish to obtain their classification accreditation in order to subdelegate authority and make decisions on classification matters. The Organization and Classification Learning and Accreditation Curriculum (GCpedia) requires prerequisites for each step of the accreditation process.
title_fr: Introduction à l'organisation et à la classification (COR133)
description_fr:
Conformément à la Directive sur la classification, une formation est nécessaire pour s'assurer que les décisions relatives à la classification sont bien gérées et sont prises dans l'intérêt public. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre est la première étape de la formation et de l'accréditation obligatoires des fonctionnaires travaillant et se spécialisant dans la classification. Les participants apprendront les notions de classification et de conception organisationnelle, le rôle et les responsabilités des principaux acteurs, la portée des demandes d'intervention en matière de classification et l'incidence des décisions concernant la classification et des modifications de la structure organisationnelle et des descriptions de travail.

Sujets traités :

·       explorer la classification; ·       examiner la conception organisationnelle; ·       évaluer les descriptions de travail; ·       comprendre l'incidence des décisions en matière de classification.

Remarques :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

Ce cours fait partie de la formation obligatoire et doit être suivi par tous les gestionnaires qui autorisent les structures organisationnelles ou les organigrammes, approuvent les descriptions d'emploi et/ou autorisent les demandes de mesure de classification. Tous les nouveaux gestionnaires qui exercent uniquement des responsabilités déléguées en matière de classification devront suivre cette formation dans les six mois suivant leur entrée en fonction, conformément à la Directive sur la formation obligatoire.

Ce cours est aussi obligatoire pour les stagiaires en organisation et classification qui souhaitent obtenir leur accréditation en classification. Celle-ci est nécessaire pour subdéléguer des pouvoirs de classification et avoir le droit de prendre des décisions de classification dans un service. Le Curriculum d'apprentissage et d'accréditation en organisation et classification (GCpédia) exige des préalables pour chaque étape du processus d'accréditation.

title_en: HR-to-Pay for Managers (COR137)
description_en:
Managers play a crucial role in making timely and accurate decisions related to human resources (HR) actions that affect employee pay. This course for managers presents realistic scenarios that explain their managerial responsibilities for respecting HR-to-pay practices and timelines. Participants will learn about the policy instruments, tools and resources in place to help them to make appropriate and informed decisions that lead to employee pay.

Topics include:

·        identifying the responsibilities, tools and processes needed to initiate pay-related actions

·        applying the appropriate acts, policies, directives, and collective agreements that support HR-to-pay decisions

·        using practical tools and job aids

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.

This course is intended for managers with signing authority under section 34 of the Financial Administration Act, as well as timekeepers, supervisors and human resources specialists who complete critical tasks that impact employee pay.
title_fr: RH à la paye pour les gestionnaires (COR137)
description_fr:
Les gestionnaires jouent un rôle crucial lorsque des décisions opportunes et éclairées doivent être prises au sujet de mesures de ressources humaines (RH) ayant une incidence sur la paye des employés. Ce cours destiné aux gestionnaires présente des mises en situation réalistes qui portent sur les responsabilités de ces derniers en ce qui concerne le respect des pratiques et des délais en matière de RH à la paye. Les participants apprendront sur les instruments de politique, les outils et les ressources dont ils disposent pour prendre des décisions judicieuses qui permettent aux employés d'être payés.

Sujets traités :

·        connaître les responsabilités, les outils et les processus permettant de prendre des mesures liées à la paye;

·        appliquer les lois, les politiques, les directives et les conventions collectives à la prise de décisions en matière de RH à la paye;

·       utiliser des outils pratiques et des outils de travail.

Remarques :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

Ce cours s'adresse aux gestionnaires ayant un pouvoir de signature en vertu de l'article 34 de la Loi sur la gestion des finances publiques, ainsi qu'aux responsables de la comptabilisation du temps, aux superviseurs et aux spécialistes des ressources humaines qui accomplissent des tâches essentielles ayant une incidence sur la paye des employés.
