title_en: Training for Learning Facilitators (COR138)
description_en:
The Canada School of Public Service actively recruits facilitators with knowledge and experience in all aspects of public service administration. This training introduces best practices, facilitation techniques, and classroom management skills for preparing and delivering both in-person and virtual learning sessions. Participants will be presented with opportunities to observe, interact with, and learn from their peers while also engaging with an audience of learners.

 

Topics include:

- reviewing adult learning principles
- developing effective strategies for engaging learners
- practising facilitation in a virtual environment, including using a web conferencing platform
- exploring facilitation techniques and classroom management skills for traditional and virtual learning settings

 

Notes:

 

This course is offered exclusively to new learning facilitators recruited by the Canada School of Public Service.

 

The total time commitment for completing this training is about 28 hours: 15 hours of virtual-instructor-led time and 13 hours of individual self-study.

 

At the end of the training, participants will be required to prepare and deliver a sample lesson to demonstrate their facilitation, presentation, and communication skills. This will be assessed and must be successfully completed in order to pass the training.

 

For instructions on how to indicate your interest in becoming a faculty member at the Canada School of Public Service, please visit Become a faculty member.

 

Schedule:

Pre-course information session (1 week before the training start date):

- How to prepare for the training
- How to get the most out of the training
- Technical requirements

 

Pre-course activities:

Pre-course activities require about 2 hours of self-study on your own time to complete.

 

Week 1:

- Modules 1 to 4
- Introduction and Expectations
- Using a Web Conferencing Platform
- Exploring Adult Learning Principles
- Facilitating Virtually

 

Time commitment: 8 hours of mandatory virtual instructor-led training plus about 7 hours of self-study

 

Week 2:

- Modules 5 and 6
- Creating a Positive Environment
- Facilitating with Accessibility in Mind


- Optional practice sessions
- Preparing for your final evaluation

 

Time commitment: 4 hours of mandatory virtual instructor-led training, 3 hours of self-study, and about 3 hours preparation for the final evaluation; optional practice sessions and office hours are also available for additional support

 

Week 3:

- Module 7
- Final Evaluation

 

Time commitment: 3 hours minimum to complete the final evaluation; some participants may also choose to attend and observe the sample lessons their peers deliver
title_fr: Formation destinée aux personnes facilitatrices d'apprentissage (COR138)
description_fr:
L’École de la fonction publique du Canada travaille activement à recruter des personnes facilitatrices ayant des connaissances et une expérience de tous les aspects de l’administration publique. Cette formation présente des pratiques exemplaires, des techniques de facilitation et des compétences de gestion de salle de classe qui permettent de préparer et d’offrir des séances en personne et en mode virtuel. Les personnes participantes pourront apprendre auprès de leurs pairs, les voir à l’œuvre et interagir avec des apprenants et apprenantes.

 

Sujets traités :

- examiner les principes de l’apprentissage chez les adultes;
- formuler des stratégies efficaces pour stimuler l’intérêt en classe;
- s’exercer à la facilitation de cours virtuels, notamment en utilisant une plateforme de webconférence;
- étudier les techniques de facilitation et de gestion de classe à utiliser dans les classes traditionnelles et virtuelles.

 

Remarques :

Ce cours est offert exclusivement aux nouvelles personnes facilitatrices de l’École de la fonction publique du Canada.

 

Au total, la formation est d’une durée d’environ 28 heures, soit 15 heures de formation virtuelle avec facilitation et 13 heures d’apprentissage individuel à rythme libre.

 

À la fin de la formation, les participants et participantes devront préparer et animer une courte séance pour mettre en évidence leurs compétences de facilitation, de présentation et de communication. Cette séance sera évaluée et sa réussite est obligatoire à l’achèvement du cours.

 

Pour savoir comment manifester votre intérêt à vous joindre au corps professoral de l’École de la fonction publique du Canada, consultez la page Devenir membre du corps professoral.

 

Horaire :

Séance d’information préalable au cours (une semaine avant le début de la formation) :

- se préparer à la formation;
- tirer pleinement profit de la formation;
- exigences en matière d’équipement.

 

Activités préalables au cours :

 

Les activités préalables au cours exigeront environ deux heures de votre temps et se font à rythme libre.

title_en: Authority Delegation Training: Managing People Effectively (COR152)
description_en:
Effective people management is a critical skill in ensuring a high-performing workforce that embodies public sector values and provides good governance and service to Canadians. This online self-paced course provides managers at all levels with the basic knowledge required to exercise their delegated human resources (HR) responsibilities within the public service. Participants will acquire the foundational understanding needed to make informed and strategic human resources-related decisions

Topics include: ·        understanding the role of organization and classification in HR management ·        planning human resources and staffing responsibly ·        recognizing responsibilities related to diversity, equity and inclusion ·        managing labour relations issues ·        respecting official languages rights and responsibilities

Notes: 

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.

This course is part of the Authority Delegation Training (ADT) program that is mandatory for managers with delegated signing authority. Delegated managers must complete the following three ADT courses, ideally in this order:

1. Authority Delegation Training: Using Public Funds Responsibly (G380)


1. Authority Delegation Training: Practising Responsible Procurement (G381)
2. Authority Delegation Training: Managing People Effectively (G382)

These courses are also open to all public servants for professional development purposes. However, completing these courses and their assessments does not entitle these learners to exercise signing authority. Consult the Directive on Delegation of Spending and Financial Authorities for the specific responsibilities for delegating, maintaining and managing, and overseeing spending and financial authorities.

Learn more about the Authority Delegation Training Program.
title_fr: Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Gérer les personnes de manière efficace (COR152)
description_fr:
La gestion efficace des personnes est une compétence essentielle pour assurer une main-d'œuvre qui offre un haut rendement, qui incarne les valeurs du secteur public et qui assure une bonne gouvernance et un bon service aux Canadiens. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre fournit aux gestionnaires de tous les niveaux les connaissances de base nécessaires pour exercer les responsabilités qui leur sont déléguées en matière de ressources humaines (RH) à la fonction publique. Les participants acquerront la compréhension fondamentale nécessaire pour prendre des décisions éclairées et stratégiques en matière de ressources humaines.

Sujets traités : ·        comprendre le rôle de l'organisation et de la classification dans la gestion des RH; ·        planifier les ressources humaines et la dotation de manière responsable; ·        reconnaître les responsabilités liées à la diversité, à l'équité et à l'inclusion; ·        gérer les questions de relations de travail; ·        respecter les droits et les responsabilités en matière de langues officielles.

Remarques : 

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

Ce cours fait partie du programme Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs (FDP), qui est obligatoire pour les gestionnaires à qui des pouvoirs de signature ont été délégués. Ces gestionnaires doivent suivre les trois cours de la FDP, idéalement dans l'ordre suivant :

1. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Utiliser les fonds publics de manière responsable (G380)


1. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Pratiquer l'approvisionnement responsable (G381)
2. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Gérer les personnes de manière efficace (G382)

Ces cours sont également ouverts à l'ensemble des fonctionnaires à des fins de perfectionnement professionnel. Toutefois, le fait de suivre ces cours et de passer les évaluations correspondantes ne donne en aucun cas à ces fonctionnaires le droit d'exercer un quelconque pouvoir de signature. Consultez la Directive sur la délégation des pouvoirs de dépenser et des pouvoirs financiers pour connaître les responsabilités particulières en matière de délégation, de maintien et de gestion, et de surveillance des pouvoirs de dépenser et des pouvoirs financiers.

Apprenez-en plus au sujet du Programme de formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs.

title_en: Financial Statement Analysis for Non-financial Professionals (COR202)

title_en: Applying Key Concepts in Financial Management (COR210)
description_en:
Understanding the fundamental rules and regulations that govern financial management frameworks is an essential component of the financial curriculum. This course connects the theory covered in Key Concepts in Financial Management (COR216) with the more practical aspects of public financial management, and is mandatory training for financial officers. Through application exercises, participants will be introduced to the tools currently used to manage finances within the federal government.

Topics include:

·       using government reports in making budgetary changes ·       making changes to program budgets partway through the financial cycle ·       reviewing variance reports ·       applying a delegation of spending chart to financial processes

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for financial officers.

This course is divided into two 3-hour sessions offered over two consecutive days.

Key Concepts in Financial Management (COR216) or Financial Management Systems (COR213) (now archived) are prerequisites and must be completed prior to registering for COR210.

title_fr: Mise en application des principaux concepts en gestion financière (COR210)
description_fr:

Ce cours obligatoire pour les agents financiers vise à faire le lien entre la théorie présentée dans le cours Principaux concepts en gestion financière (COR216) et les aspects plus pratiques de la gestion des finances publiques. Les participants se familiariseront, à l'aide d'exercices pratiques, avec les outils couramment utilisés dans la gestion financière au sein du gouvernement fédéral.

Sujets traités :

- se servir des rapports gouvernementaux pour apporter des modifications budgétaires;
- modifier les budgets des programmes au milieu du cycle financier;
- examiner des rapports sur les écarts;
- utiliser un tableau de délégation des pouvoirs de dépenser dans le cadre des processus financiers.

Remarques :

title_en: Master Class on Strategic Resourcing (COR215)
description_en:
The financial resources of the Government of Canada are safeguarded through balanced controls that enable flexibility and manage risk. This course for seasoned executives examines the principles and processes behind strategic resourcing and financial management, as well as the important role played by central agencies. Through practical workshops, participants will explore challenges, reflect on current practices and engage with colleagues to identify best practices for effectively securing the resources needed to deliver on their organizational mandate.

 

Topics include: 

- examining accountability and stewardship 


- managing finances and achieving results
- seeking authorizations and securing resources
- reporting on results and measuring performance
- advocating for proper financial resources

 

Notes: 

This course is delivered as two consecutive days of training. Registration is reserved for employees at the EX-02 and EX-03 levels. A short readiness questionnaire will be administered prior to the offering date to enable full participation in class discussions.

 

A valid Authority Delegation Validation Assessment for Executives (COR254) certificate is a required prerequisite for this course. Certifications are valid for five years.

 

Executive employees registering for COR215 are encouraged to also complete the Authority Delegation Training: Using Public Funds Responsibly (COR250) to refresh their understanding of the core principles of financial management.

 

To express your interest in participating in this course, please submit a readiness questionnaire.

title_fr: Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Utiliser les fonds publics de manière responsable (COR250)
description_fr:
Les gestionnaires de la fonction publique fédérale sont censés comprendre les pouvoirs financiers qui leur sont délégués. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre destiné aux gestionnaires de tous les niveaux présente un aperçu des pratiques attendues pour assurer la saine gestion des fonds publics au moyen d'une planification, d'une gestion des dépenses et d'une production de rapports responsables. Par l'étude d'exemples utiles, les participants apprendront à exercer les pouvoirs financiers qui leur sont délégués conformément aux politiques, aux pratiques et aux procédures du gouvernement.

Sujets traités :

·       élaborer un plan de travail et un budget; ·       produire des rapports sur les finances et les résultats; ·       exercer des pouvoirs financiers et de dépenser délégués.

Remarques :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

Ce cours fait partie du programme Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs (FDP), qui est obligatoire pour les gestionnaires à qui des pouvoirs de signature ont été délégués. Ces gestionnaires doivent suivre les trois cours de la FDP, idéalement dans l'ordre suivant :

1. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Utiliser les fonds publics de manière responsable (G380)


1. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Pratiquer l'approvisionnement responsable (G381)
2. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Gérer les personnes de manière efficace (G382)

Ces cours sont également ouverts à l'ensemble des fonctionnaires à des fins de perfectionnement professionnel. Toutefois, le fait de suivre ces cours et de passer les évaluations correspondantes ne donne en aucun cas à ces fonctionnaires le droit d'exercer un quelconque pouvoir de signature. Consultez la Directive sur la délégation des pouvoirs de dépenser et des pouvoirs financiers pour connaître les responsabilités particulières en matière de délégation, de maintien et de gestion, et de surveillance des pouvoirs de dépenser et des pouvoirs financiers.

Apprenez-en plus au sujet du Programme de formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs.

title_en: Business Continuity Management: Conducting a Business Impact Analysis (COR312)
description_en:
To ensure the continued delivery of critical operations during emergencies, federal organizations must plan for potential service disruptions by conducting a business impact analysis (BIA). This online self-paced course explains how to conduct a BIA using the Government of Canada’s official methodology, as outlined in its Business Continuity Management Program Guide (2023). Participants will learn how to identify BIA components, communicate their value and align their work with federal business continuity management practices.

Topics Include:

·       facilitating a business impact analysis

·       identifying the diverse roles and responsibilities in the business continuity management (BCM) process

·       applying the Government of Canada’s official business impact analysis methodology

·       analyzing the criticality of services and delivery requirements

Notes:

This course offers two pathways tailored to different roles in business continuity management:

 

Pathway 1: BCM Specialist Pathway (4 hours): Designed for those leading and facilitating the BIA process as part of a BCM program. Ideal for BCM specialists and coordinators seeking in-depth knowledge of the Government of Canada’s BIA methodology and application.

·       Intended audience: BCM functional specialists and coordinators

 

Pathway 2: BIA Participant Pathway (2 hours): Designed for those contributing to the BIA process. Ideal for individuals looking to build foundational knowledge to assess the criticality of services and identify critical service delivery requirements.

·       Intended audience: Service owners, subject-matter experts, chief security officers, deputy chief security officers, individuals responsible for related resilience disciplines, general staff.
title_fr: La gestion de la continuité des activités : réalisation d’une analyse des incidences sur les activités (COR312)
description_fr:
Afin d’assurer l’exécution continue des activités essentielles en situation d’urgence, les organisations fédérales doivent se préparer à d’éventuelles perturbations des services en réalisant une analyse des incidences sur les activités (AIA). Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre explique comment effectuer une AIA selon la méthodologie officielle du gouvernement du Canada, décrite dans l’édition de 2023 du Guide du programme de gestion de la continuité des activités. Les participants apprendront à cerner les éléments d’une AIA, à communiquer leur valeur et à suivre les pratiques fédérales en matière de gestion de la continuité des activités.

Sujets traités :

·       faciliter la réalisation d’une analyse des incidences sur les activités;

·       connaître les divers rôles et responsabilités liés au processus de gestion de la continuité des activités (GCA);

·       utiliser la méthodologie officielle du gouvernement du Canada en matière d’analyse des incidences sur les activités;

·       analyser le caractère essentiel des services et les exigences liées à leur prestation.

Remarques :

Ce cours offre deux cheminements, chacun adapté à différents rôles dans la gestion de la continuité des activités.

Cheminement 1 : Spécialistes de la GCA (4 heures) : Conçu pour les personnes qui dirigent et facilitent le processus d’AIA dans le cadre d’un programme de GCA. Ce cheminement est idéal pour les spécialistes et les coordonnateurs de la GCA qui cherchent à acquérir des connaissances approfondies sur la méthodologie du gouvernement du Canada en matière d’AIA et sur son application.

·       Public cible : spécialistes fonctionnels et coordonnateurs de la GCA


Cheminement 2 : Participants à la GCA (2 heures) : Conçu pour les personnes qui contribuent au processus d’AIA. Ce cheminement est idéal pour les personnes qui cherchent à acquérir des connaissances de base en vue d’évaluer le caractère essentiel des services et de cerner les exigences en matière de prestation des services essentiels.

·       Public cible : propriétaires de services, experts en la matière, dirigeants principaux de la sécurité, dirigeants principaux adjoints de la sécurité, personnes responsables de disciplines connexes contribuant à la résilience, personnel général

title_en: Developing a Statement of Work and Evaluation Criteria (COR407)
description_en:
Departments and agencies use a variety of solicitation methods to acquire goods and services through competitive contracts. This course covers two critical elements of the solicitation process: the statement of work and the evaluation criteria for bids submitted. Participants will learn how to write proper requirements to obtain their desired product or service and how to set evaluation criteria that will help select the appropriate bidder.

title_en: Indigenous Considerations in Procurement (COR409)
description_en:
There are many ways contracting authorities can support economic growth for Indigenous businesses, people and communities. This online self-paced course introduces the federal procurement policies, obligations and considerations that can be applied to increase opportunities for Indigenous businesses in Canada. Participants will learn about the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) and gain a broader understanding of modern treaties or Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs) and how they can affect the procurement process.

Topics include:

· determining the applicability of modern treaties/CLCAs and the key mechanisms of the PSIB

· describing the common procurement obligations that may apply when a procurement is subject to a modern treaty/CLCA

· explaining how modern treaty/CLCA obligations and the use of the PSIB may affect certain steps in the procurement process

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for procurement specialists.
title_fr: Considérations autochtones en matière d'approvisionnement (COR409)
description_fr:
Les autorités contractantes disposent de nombreux moyens pour favoriser la croissance économique des Autochtones, y compris de leurs entreprises et collectivités. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente les politiques et les obligations fédérales ainsi que les aspects à prendre en considération en matière d'approvisionnement afin d'accroître les occasions pour les entreprises autochtones au Canada. Les participants se familiariseront avec la Stratégie d'approvisionnement auprès des entreprises autochtones (SAEA) et acquerront une meilleure compréhension des traités modernes ou ententes sur les revendications territoriales globales (ERTG) et de leur incidence sur le processus d'approvisionnement.

Sujets traités :

· déterminer si des traités modernes/ERTG et les principaux mécanismes de la SAEA s'appliquent;

· décrire les obligations courantes qui s'appliquent lorsqu'un approvisionnement est assujetti à un traité moderne/ERTG;

· expliquer de quelle façon les obligations liées aux traités modernes/ERTG et l'application de la SAEA peuvent influer sur certaines étapes du processus d'approvisionnement.

Remarques :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les spécialistes de l’approvisionnement.

title_en: Procurement in the Nunavut Settlement Area (COR410)
description_en:
To fulfill its obligations under Article 24 of the Nunavut Agreement, the Government of Canada has issued the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases in the Nunavut Settlement Area, known as the "Nunavut Directive." This online self-paced course provides an overview of the Nunavut Directive and outlines the measures by which procurement specialists must provide fair and reasonable opportunities for Inuit firms to submit bids on government contracts. Participants will learn about the key policy measures of this directive and how to apply them during the procurement process. 

Topics include: 

· identifying when a procurement is subject to the Nunavut Directive 

· limiting bids to Inuit firms depending on market capacity (as per the Inuit Firm Registry) 

· including bid evaluation criteria related to benefits for Inuit and Nunavut, either on a best-effort or mandatory basis, depending on contract value 

· determining how to document and report on government contracts (as per the Nunavut Directive)

description_en:
To support Canada's goal of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions, federal facilities have committed to taking practical steps to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions from their operations. This online self-paced course provides an overview of the deep energy retrofit process and its adoption by federal organizations. title_en: Energy Efficiency Expert Evaluations (COR414)
description_en:
Energy Efficiency Expert Evaluation is a multidisciplinary evaluation process for identifying and implementing low-cost solutions to improving operational performance and reducing energy costs. This online self-paced course provides an introduction to managing Energy Efficiency Expert Evaluations (E4s) in federal facilities. Participants will be introduced to the basic tools required to conduct E4 inspections of government buildings and other facilities and learn how to develop practical solutions to improve their efficiency.

title_fr: Évaluations d'experts de l'efficacité énergétique (COR414)
description_fr:
L'évaluation de l'efficacité énergétique par des experts est un processus d'évaluation multidisciplinaire qui permet de trouver et de mettre en œuvre des solutions peu coûteuses visant à améliorer le rendement opérationnel et à réduire les coûts énergétiques. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre offre une introduction à la gestion des évaluations de l'efficacité énergétique par des experts dans les immeubles fédéraux. Les participants se familiariseront avec les outils de base requis pour mener des inspections de ce type dans les immeubles fédéraux et d'autres bâtiments, et ils apprendront comment trouver des solutions pratiques pour être plus efficaces.
 
Sujets traités :
 
·      gérer les quatre étapes de l'évaluation de l'efficacité énergétique par des experts : planification, découverte, mesures correctrices et transfert;
·      découvrir les causes profondes des problèmes de rendement énergétique;
·      comprendre la différence entre mise en service, mise en service rétroactive et remise en service.
 
Remarques :
 
Ce cours, adapté à partir de matériel de formation du Federal Energy Management Program (département de l'Énergie des États-Unis), est donné par les Services pour un gouvernement vert de Ressources naturelles Canada.

title_en: Information Management in the Digital Age (COR506)
description_en:
Canada, like most other countries, is experiencing a rapid transformation in the delivery of digital services and must keep pace with expectations. This course explains the roles of the information management (IM) community and the new program delivery techniques outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition. Through a blend of self-paced and virtual instructor-led learning, participants will explore the main trends influencing the field of information management and the IM activities that are supporting the government's transformation towards providing secure and modern digital services.

This course builds on the knowledge and skills acquired in Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) and focuses on applying information management in the digital age, as outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition.

Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) is a prerequisite.

description_en:

This course provides a practical guide to the information management (IM) methods, tools and activities that support an effective departmental IM program. Participants will learn how to use a function-based classification structure, establish retention specifications and follow the proper process for disposing of information resources.

• applying function-based methodologies

description_fr:

Ce cours présente de façon concrète les méthodes, les outils et les activités de gestion de l'information (GI) qui favorisent l'efficacité des programmes ministériels de GI. Les participants apprendront à utiliser une structure de classification basée sur les fonctions, à établir des critères de conservation et à suivre les démarches appropriées pour éliminer des ressources documentaires.

Sujets traités :

• appliquer des méthodes axées sur les fonctions; 

• consigner les pratiques et les procédures; 

• établir des critères de conservation afin de simplifier le processus de disposition.

Le cours La gestion de l'information à l'appui des programmes et des services (I230) est un préalable à ce cours.

Ce cours est divisé en trois séances de 3 heures réparties sur une semaine.

title_en: Introduction to Cyber Security Management (DDN106)
description_en:
Security practitioners are expected to have a basic understanding of information technology (IT) security programs and what is involved in managing them. This online self-paced course provides an overview of common IT security program activities in the Government of Canada and introduces the legal, policy, business and threat contexts for IT security. By gaining a renewed appreciation for the IT security context and program activities, participants will be better able to support IT security priorities across the Government of Canada.

Topics include:

• defining the IT security context • identifying IT security program activities • supporting IT security priorities

Notes:

This course is delivered by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security. To register, or to sign in or create an account, visit the Cyber Centre Learning Hub and search for the course by title or by code ITS101S.
title_fr: Introduction à la gestion des risques liés à la cybersécurité (DDN106)
description_fr:
Les spécialistes de la sécurité sont tenus de posséder des connaissances de base sur les programmes de sécurité des technologies de l'information (TI) et sur les éléments qui entrent en jeu dans leur gestion. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre offre un aperçu des activités qui sont couramment réalisées dans le cadre des programmes de sécurité des TI du gouvernement du Canada, en plus de présenter les aspects juridiques, politiques et opérationnels de la sécurité des TI ainsi que les menaces qui pèsent sur celle-ci. Les participants seront mieux à même d'appuyer les priorités liées à la sécurité des TI à l'échelle du gouvernement du Canada s'ils s'intéressent davantage au contexte de la sécurité des TI et aux activités des programmes.

title_en: Network Security Threats and Their Impact (DDN109)
description_en:
Despite advancements in IT security, many organizations remain subject to frequent and sophisticated network attacks. This online self-paced course investigates the most common types of network security threats, including how to prevent them and how to detect them if your system is breached. Participants will learn about the importance of stopping hackers from accessing vital data by addressing system weaknesses that can be exploited by potential attackers.

Topics include:

• understanding why network security threats are important
• outlining a typical ransomware attack
• countering and mitigating threats to network security
• exploring social engineering, malware and other types of security threats

title_en: Learning from Failure (DDN111)
description_en:
Failure is a natural part of life and business and should be embraced as an opportunity to learn and grow. This online self-paced course describes the cycle of success when developing people and their talent, which includes failure and strategies for embracing it. Participants will explore key actions that foster an attitude of continuous learning and will discover the potential benefits of failure and other setbacks.

•	defining the three types of failure

•	fostering an attitude of learning from failure

•	recognizing the growth opportunities that can come from embracing failure

•	turning a failure into a learning opportunity

Artificial intelligence has quickly become an inescapable part of the modern digital landscape by driving new possibilities across almost all domains. This online self-paced course introduces the core concepts of artificial intelligence, how it is currently being used, and how to use AI responsibly within the federal public service. Participants will expand their knowledge of AI, its present-day limitations, as well as the ethical considerations of its potential and future use.

Topics include:

- analyzing where and how AI is used
- applying the principles of responsible AI
- describing the relationship between AI and data
- recognizing the challenges and ethical considerations of AI

title_en: GC Cloud for Managers and Executives: Planning for GC Cloud (DDN211)
description_en:
All managers and executives have a role to play in making decisions about the use of cloud technologies and adopting them within their organization. This online self-paced course focuses on the fundamentals of using GC Cloud as a business decision, and the importance of proper planning prior to its implementation. By reviewing common financial and IT considerations, participants will learn to recognize the value of GC Cloud and the role of having a sound plan to help guide its integration.

Topics include:

•   recognizing the value proposition of GC Cloud

•   busting cloud myths

•   starting the cloud adoption journey

title_en: Connecting with the Internet of Things (DDN215)
description_en:
The Internet of Things is an interrelated system that allows people to connect with physical objects, devices, machines and everyday objects, and allows those things to connect with each other. This online self-paced course covers the basics of the Internet of Things (IoT), including its business applications and its value to customers, organizations and everyday life. Participants will learn how to transform information into value, generate revenue, and revolutionize the way their business provides value to its customers.   Topics include:

- understanding the purpose and ideas behind the IoT
- identifying key IoT data management challenges
- transforming information into value
- generating revenue from the IoT
- connecting with customers through the IoT

title_en: Creating Engagement with Virtual Reality (DDN216)
description_en:
In recent years, virtual reality has made major strides due to the contributions of artificial intelligence and 3-D technologies. This online self-paced course examines the characteristics of virtual reality (VR) and its many different business applications, as well as the equipment typically used for both mobile and high-powered VR experiences. description_en:
Artificial Intelligence has the potential to revolutionize the way businesses and industries operate. This online self-paced course examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in business and explores common cognitive technologies that use AI and the effects of its applications in the workplace. title_en: Digital Accelerator - Design Thinking Boot Camp (DDN222)
description_en:
The design thinking process is a problem-solving methodology for complex problems that is based on five core stages: empathize, define, ideate, prototype, and test. This course (boot camp) offers an immersive multi-day learning experience in which individuals or established work teams can explore new ways of working while advancing their digital and collaboration skills. Guided by in-class facilitators, participants will apply the design thinking process to a real-world government work scenario that requires human-centred approaches to address policy, product and service challenges.


Topics include:


- explaining problem framing and scoping
- applying multi-perspective user-centred research methods
- conducting data analysis and synthesis
- brainstorming and ideating
- prototyping, testing and user experience reporting


Notes:


Upon completion of this boot camp, participants will have gained practical experience in applying design and delivery principles, in collaborating with their peers, and in making user-centred and evidence-based decisions using work methods that are scalable and iterative.

title_en: Inclusive by Design: Applying the GC Digital Standards and Gender-based Analysis Plus (DDN223)
description_en:
Inclusive design is an intentional design process that recognizes diversity and uses inclusive approaches that ensure more equitable outcomes. This online self-paced course identifies the impact of personal and organizational biases on decisions at work, and explores how to make interactions more inclusive by applying Gender-based Analysis Plus (GBA Plus) and the Government of Canada’s Digital Standards. Participants will be provided with job aids to help them integrate inclusive solutions into the development of government programs and services.

 

Topics include:

 

·         recognizing the impact of personal and organizational biases

·         using the GC Digital Standards and GBA Plus to mitigate biases

·         eliminating potential barriers when developing products and services

 

Notes:

 

This course offers a high-level overview of bias, the GC Digital Standards, and GBA Plus and refers participants to detailed learning resources. The course includes downloadable content that combines key considerations from the GC Digital Standards and GBA Plus to assist in the preparation of an inclusion analysis.
title_fr: Conception inclusive : appliquer les normes numériques du GC et l'analyse comparative entre les sexes plus (DDN223)
description_fr:
La conception inclusive est un processus de conception qui permet de reconnaître la diversité et d’utiliser des approches inclusives de manière intentionnelle pour assurer des résultats plus équitables. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente les effets que les biais personnels et organisationnels ont sur les décisions prises au travail, et permet d’explorer comment appliquer les Normes relatives au numérique du gouvernement du Canada et l’analyse comparative entre les sexes plus (ACS Plus) pour rendre les interactions plus inclusives. Les participants recevront des outils de travail qui les aideront à intégrer des solutions inclusives dans l’élaboration des programmes et services gouvernementaux.

 

Sujets traités :

 

·         reconnaître les effets des biais personnels et organisationnels;

·         utiliser les Normes relatives au numérique du GC et l’ACS Plus pour atténuer les biais;

·         éliminer les obstacles potentiels lors de l’élaboration de produits et de services.

 

Remarques :

 

Ce cours offre un aperçu des biais cognitifs, des Normes relatives au numérique du GC et de l’ACS Plus, tout en renvoyant les participants à des ressources d’apprentissage détaillées. On y présente du contenu téléchargeable qui combine les considérations clés découlant des Normes relatives au numérique du GC et de l’ACS Plus pour aider à la réalisation d’une analyse de l’inclusion.

Topics include:

• seizing tomorrow's opportunities today 

• rethinking organizational business models to enable digital transformation

title_en: Exploring Customer Journey Mapping (DDN226)
description_en:
Customer journey mapping can help to better identify your customers' needs and their common pain points. This online self-paced course introduces the customer journey map, a helpful problem-solving tool used to document every step of the customer experience. By creating their own map, participants will learn how to better understand their customers' needs, identify the problems they encounter, and brainstorm effective solutions.

Topics include:

• identifying the benefits of customer journey mapping
• setting the business goal and establishing a mapping team
• drafting, updating and completing a customer journey map
• prioritizing solutions to improve customer focus
• avoiding common mapping mistakes

title_en: Cyber Security Fundamentals (DDN231)
description_en:
Knowing the basics of cyber security is beneficial to all government employees, especially to those who work with or support IT security professionals. This online instructor-led course provides an introduction to cyber security basics and the cyber threat landscape. Through a mix of lectures, discussions, examples and group activities, participants will explore cyber security terminology, concepts and processes, including the tools, tactics and procedures of cyber threat actors.

Topics include:

- reviewing the goals and challenges of cyber security
- exploring the cyber threat landscape and the security controls that can mitigate vulnerabilities
- explaining how the internet functions
- understanding the threat context and common vulnerabilities
- applying cyber security concepts to a compromise scenario

Notes:

title_en: Cyber Security in the GC for Home and Telework (DDN232)
description_en:
When working outside the secured work environment of a government office, employees are expected to take proactive measures to protect their work files from exposure to cyber threats. This online instructor-led course explores basic cyber security concepts and home network essentials, including system settings that can reduce online exposure to cyber security threats when teleworking. Participants will learn to apply the Communications Security Establishment's Top Ten IT Security Actions to protect information on their home network or mobile devices.

Topics include:

- updating system settings to reduce the exposure of private information
- storing sensitive information on a home network
- installing industry standard protective software
- adopting countermeasures to cyber security threats
- reacting to security breaches or incidents

title_en: Online Privacy and Identity Management (DDN233)
description_en:
Employees working in online environments face increased privacy and cyber security concerns stemming from both their professional and personal online activities. This course provides an overview of the online privacy landscape and recommends strategies for minimizing potential threats and managing one’s online identity. Participants will learn how to assess their digital footprint and identify best practices for managing and protecting their online identity.


Topics include:


·       increasing awareness of cyber security concerns linked to privacy

·       identifying tools and procedures to enhance digital privacy

·       providing a forward outlook on identity management


Notes:


This course is delivered by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and has a cost of $750. To register and pay, or to sign in or create an account, visit the Cyber Centre Learning Hub and search for the course by title or by code CYB103C.

title_fr: La vie privée et la gestion de l'identité en ligne (DDN233)
description_fr:
Les employés qui travaillent en ligne éprouvent un nombre croissant de préoccupations liées à la protection de la vie privée et à la cybersécurité qui découlent auteur de leurs activités professionnelles que personnelles. Ce cours fournit un aperçu du paysage de la protection de la vie privée en ligne et propose des stratégies pour contrer les menaces et gérer son identité en ligne. Les participants apprendront à évaluer leur empreinte numérique et découvriront des pratiques exemplaires pour gérer et protéger leur identité en ligne.


Sujets traités :


·       apprendre à mieux connaître les préoccupations en matière de cybersécurité liées à la protection de la vie privée;

·       connaître les outils et les procédures visant à améliorer la protection des renseignements personnels numériques;

·       offrir des perspectives concernant la gestion de l’identité.


Remarques :


Ce cours est offert par le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité au coût de 750 $. Pour vous inscrire au cours et le payer, ou pour ouvrir une session ou créer un compte, visitez le Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité et faites une recherche en utilisant le titre du cours ou le code CYB103C.


Sur demande, ce cours peut être adapté à des groupes en fonction de leurs objectifs d'apprentissage professionnels ou encore de ceux de leur entreprise ou de leur ministère. Pour obtenir plus de renseignements sur ce service et sur ses coûts, écrivez au Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité, à education@cyber.gc.ca.

This online self-paced course explores different ways to monitor social media and highlights how social intelligence can improve organizational performance. Participants will learn best practices for gathering and analyzing social media data, and insightful ways to use social awareness strategies to deliver real business value.

Topics include:

- defining the business benefits of social intelligence
- setting up effective social media monitoring
- identifying the common sources of social media data
- analyzing social data effectively to uncover real business intelligence
- applying social intelligence findings strategically

title_en: Discover Cyber Security (DDN235)
description_en:
Digital technologies have quickly become an integral part of our daily lives, with new developments and security concerns emerging every day. This online self-paced course helps to build a greater awareness and understanding of the reality of cyber risks by exploring common security vulnerabilities and cyber threats, such as malware, password attacks and social engineering. Participants will learn to recognize potential threats and how to protect themselves, their digital information and the systems they use.

Topics include:

· defining cyber security and its importance

· protecting against malware and other cyber threats

· understanding Government of Canada security roles and policies

· adopting best practices

· pursuing additional security training opportunities

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for employees of the core public administration.

Learners will receive a certificate of completion after successfully completing the final quiz. Revalidation is required annually by completing Cyber Security Quest (DDN247) (recommended) or by redoing DDN235.

This course is offered in collaboration with the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.

title_en: Introduction to Product Management in the Public Service (DDN236)
description_en:
An important goal of effective product management is to ensure that the product meets the needs of its intended users. This online self-paced course introduces the key concepts of product management and recommends best practices for creating products in a public service context. Participants will learn about product teams, including the different roles, responsibilities and skillsets of team members, as well as some of the tools available to assist them.

 

Topics include:

- introducing product management terminology
- guiding product development from conception to delivery
- defining the roles and responsibilities of product teams
- applying design thinking, Agile practices, and human-centred design approaches

 

Notes:

 

This course is intended for newcomers to product management in the public service, including project managers retraining as product managers, first-time product managers, product owners, and new employees working in product development teams.

The first step in the design process is to understand the problem space, which involves exploring the circumstances behind a problem. This online self-paced course presents the foundational methods and tools needed to identify and analyze problems that need solving. Participants will learn how to apply these discovery methods in their work and use sound problem framing to set up the next steps in the design process.

Topics include:

· identifying and framing the problem to be solved

· identifying the real people impacted by the problem

· exploring empathy mapping

· setting boundaries for solutions in a government context

· writing point-of-view problem statements

description_en:
Making the switch to digital technologies requires taking a close look at core business processes, organizational governance and customer experiences. This online self-paced course assembles a playbook of best practices for digital transformation that focus on the customer, mobilize operational processes and sustain the employee experience during a period of change. Participants will learn about the underlying business models and digital platforms that power digital transformation, along with the leadership capabilities required to make digital transformation a reality.

Topics include:

· focusing digital transformation on the customer experience

· recognizing the operational elements of digital transformation

· supporting business model transformation

· identifying the four major components of implementing digital transformation

description_en:
As the world and technology changes, organizations are constantly looking for new ways to adapt and transform themselves. This online self-paced course provides an overview of how to build digital dexterity within an organization to ensure its readiness for potential business opportunities. Participants will be introduced to the four characteristics of a digital organization and learn about strategies to sustain a successful digital transformation.

Topics include:

· setting strategies for building a digital-first mindset

· recognizing the common practices of digitally adept organizations

· identifying strategies for moving from a traditional to a digital organizational design

· identifying the four characteristics of digital dexterity: a digital-first mindset, digitized organizational practices, the human capabilities of an empowered digital workforce, and the resources to support it all

This online self-paced course explains the requirements for successful innovation and presents ways to lead effectively through the obstacles to its success. Participants will learn about the characteristics of an innovation culture and how to establish a flexible innovation process that encourages creativity in others.

Topics include:

· identifying the requirements for innovation success

· taking leadership actions to overcome obstacles to innovation

· recognizing the characteristics of an innovation culture

· encouraging creativity and innovation in people

· identifying the steps and activities of a flexible innovation process

title_en: Ethical Considerations in Artificial Intelligence (DDN243)
description_en:
The use of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping how services are designed and delivered across the public and private sectors. This online self-paced course explores the foundations of artificial intelligence, its opportunities, potential risks, ethical considerations and the use of AI in the public sector. Participants will review the ethical implications of AI use in government, examine examples that highlight potential risks and challenges, and learn about methods to help address them.

 

Topics include:

 

·         exploring ethical principles for the responsible development and use of AI, including fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy and security

·         exploring common applications and best practices of AI use in the public service

·         recognizing key ethical challenges and identifying strategies to minimize risks

·         reviewing emerging AI standards, regulations and governance frameworks

The final step in the design process is to prototype and test the final iterations of a product or service. This online self-paced course presents the steps to take to create and test prototypes effectively. Participants will learn about the benefits of testing prototypes, evaluation methods and tools, and how to refine a prototype into a completed product or service.

Topics include:

· explaining  why prototyping is important

· designing hypothesis-driven prototypes

· using prototypes to test and validate hypotheses

· selecting the right tools to build prototypes of various fidelity levels

title_en: Cyber Security Best Practices (DDN250)
description_en:
Digital technologies have quickly become an integral part of our daily lives, with new developments and security concerns emerging every day. This course provides an overview of the various cyber security risks and threats that may be encountered in our professional and personal lives.  Participants will learn behaviours and strategies to mitigate these risks, such as choosing strong passwords, spotting and properly handling suspicious emails, and securing personal devices and social media accounts.

Topics include:

· identifying various cyber threats

· determining strategies, recommendations, steps, and behaviours to mitigate risks online

· implementing best practices that mitigate cyber risk and improve cyber hygiene

Notes:

This course is delivered by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and has a cost of $750. To register and pay, or to sign in or create an account, visit the Cyber Centre Learning Hub and search for the course by title or by code CYB102C.

Upon request, this course can be tailored for groups to fit specific professional, business or departmental learning objectives. Email the Cyber Centre Learning Hub at education@cyber.gc.ca for specific details and costs.
title_fr: Pratiques exemplaires en matière de cybersécurité (DDN250)
description_fr:
Les technologies numériques sont rapidement devenues une partie intégrante de notre quotidien, s'accompagnant chaque jour de nouvelles avancées et préoccupations en matière de sécurité. Ce cours donne un aperçu des différents risques et menaces liés à la cybersécurité que l'on peut rencontrer dans notre vie professionnelle et personnelle. Les participants apprendront sur les comportements et les stratégies à adopter pour atténuer ces risques, comme choisir des mots de passe difficiles à deviner, repérer et traiter adéquatement les courriels suspects, et sécuriser les appareils personnels et les comptes de médias sociaux.

Sujet traités :

· reconnaître différentes cybermenaces;

· déterminer les stratégies et les comportement à adopter ainsi que les recommandations et les étapes à suivre pour atténuer les risques en ligne;

· mettre en place des pratiques exemplaires qui permettent d'atténuer les cyberrisques et d'améliorer la cyberhygiène.

Remarques :

Ce cours est offert par le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité au coût de 750 $. Pour vous inscrire au cours et le payer, ou pour ouvrir une session ou créer un compte, visitez le Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité et faites une recherche en utilisant le titre du cours ou le code CYB102C.

Sur demande, ce cours peut être adapté à des groupes en fonction de leurs objectifs d'apprentissage professionnels ou encore de ceux de leur entreprise ou de leur ministère. Pour obtenir plus de renseignements sur ce service et sur ses coûts, écrivez au Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité, à education@cyber.gc.ca.

title_en: Transforming Government Services for the Digital Era (DDN251)
description_en:
To meet the high expectations surrounding the delivery of digital services, leaders throughout the Government of Canada must upskill to help guide this digital transformation. This online self-paced course, designed for executive leaders and other forward-thinking public servants, provides insight into how government services are currently being transformed or adapted to meet the digital demands of Canadians. Participants will learn about the need to adapt their leadership style and the new skills that are required for them to succeed in the digital era. 

Topics include: 

- exploring the evolution of government services 
- examining how governments are building and supporting digital platforms and organizations 
- explaining why getting government digital services right is so important 
- developing new leadership skills for the digital era 

Notes: 

Each week for eight weeks, participants will receive an email containing advice and guidance from David Eaves, Associate Professor in Digital Government at the University College London Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose.
Each email will include a short video (between 5 to 10 minutes) and a curated list of links to resources on public service transformation and digital leadership. At the end of the eight weeks, participants who viewed the videos will receive a certificate of completion.

Participants will be equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to lead AI initiatives that drive meaningful impact, while fostering innovation and collaboration across departments.

title_en: Applying Human-Centred Design (DDN253)
description_en:
Human-centred design (HCD) is a practice that places the needs, wants and experiences of people at the core of its approach. This course takes the form of an interactive seminar that explores how human-centred design can be achieved through innovative methods such as design thinking and behavioural science to improve government services. Participants will examine relatable case studies to learn how to engage with HCD principles, behaviours and impacts and how to integrate HCD best practices into their work practices.

 

Topics include:

 

·         understanding the HCD mindset and its principles

·         exploring real Government of Canada case studies that demonstrate HCD best practices

·         engaging in the discovery, definition, ideation, prototyping and testing phases

·         designing inclusive and accessible solutions

·         applying the HCD approach to Government of Canada products and services

 

Notes:

 

This course is facilitated by Dominira Saul, a design practitioner at Dffrnt, an Ottawa-based strategic research and design consultancy that helps clients solve complex problems through creative, human-centred approaches.

title_en: Leading Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Culture in the Workplace (DDN263)
description_en:
Adopting artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly and responsibly is presenting complex challenges for public sector leaders. This course serves as a virtual and interactive seminar for executives on what it takes to adopt new AI technologies and take the actions required to enable an AI culture change in the workplace. Through thoughtful discussion and by learning from experienced leaders in this field, participants will reflect on how AI-driven change impacts people and which leadership behaviours and change-management practices can best support them within Government of Canada realities and accountabilities.

 

Topics include:

·         assessing readiness for AI adoption

·         identifying leadership actions that enable culture change

·         supporting teams through uncertainty

·         strengthening capacity for responsible AI adoption

·         improving service and program delivery through AI

 

Notes:

 

This course is delivered as a virtual seminar and is available exclusively for employees at the EX level.

title_en: Introduction to Data in the Public Service (DDN301)
description_en:
Data is at the heart of the transformative shift in modern digital government, enabling new policy decisions and enhancing public services. This course uses a peer-learning approach to explore the strategic issues related to the role and use of data in the public service in a non-technical way. Participants will have opportunities to share their awareness of and involvement in data issues, regardless of their level or comfort with the data for which they are responsible.

Topics include:

- applying commonly used data terms and concepts
- explaining how the government uses data
- recognizing why data skills are so important
- identifying one's own role with data and how it fits with other organizational roles

title_en: GC Data Demystified (DDN304)
description_en:
Understanding and working with data is essential for making evidence-based decisions in today’s digital workplace. This online self-paced course introduces the importance of data, data-related terminology and the various roles in government which commonly work with data. Through storytelling and interactive learning activities, participants will gain a better understanding of how data, the government and people in Canada are interconnected.

Topics include:

•	defining the data terminology used in the federal public service 

•	identifying the connections between government, data and the public 

•	recognizing the different roles that work with data

title_en: Big Data Fundamentals (DDN305)
description_en:
Big data describes the large volume of structured and unstructured data that organizations amass on a daily basis. This online self-paced course examines the key characteristics of big data, the types of data it incorporates, the benefits it can provide, and the different ways it can be applied. Participants will explore some of the fundamental security challenges of big data and review best practices for managing big data throughout its information life cycle.

Topics include:

•	recognizing the key characteristics of big data
•	identifying the benefits of big data to organizations
•	distinguishing between data sources and market sectors
•	applying best practices for securing big data
•	understanding the phases of the data life cycle

title_en: Making Data-Driven Decisions (DDN307)
description_en:
When used in combination with business acumen, making decisions based on data can be a powerful tool for change. This online self-paced course identifies the benefits of data-driven decision making and explores a balanced approach where decision-makers do not rely on a single perspective as the basis for making choices. Participants will learn best practices for using data to inform their decisions, including how to avoid common mistakes when interpreting data.

Topics include:

•	identifying the benefits of data-driven decision making
•	asking questions and thinking critically about data
•	creating a data-driven decision-making culture
•	reviewing the steps of the data-driven decision-making process

title_en: Exploring Data Visualization (DDN308)
description_en:
Data visualization makes sense of complex data by extracting actionable insights that can give your organization a competitive edge. This online self-paced course sets out the considerations for creating data visualizations and relaying messages with the help of data visualization tools. Participants will learn data visualization techniques and design best practices that will help to ensure their visualizations are clearly and accurately communicating what their data means.   Topics include:

- recognizing the benefits of data visualization
- choosing software to create data visualizations
- communicating clearly with data visualizations
- distinguishing between the different types of data visualizations
- avoiding the use of misleading data visualizations

title_en: Harnessing the Power of Data Science for Business Growth (DDN309)
description_en:
Data science involves using scientific analysis, tools and mathematics to extract useful business insights from raw data. This online self-paced course presents the characteristics and key elements of data science and explores the potential benefits of data science to the organizations that utilize it. Participants will learn about the skill sets needed on a data management team, and discover best practices for extracting useful insights from data to guide decisions and drive business improvements.   Topics include:

- exploring how data science can increase business value
- identifying the three key elements of the data science process
- developing a data science team with the required skill sets
- extracting useful insights from raw data
- reviewing the common challenges of using data science

title_en: Principles of Data Ethics (DDN312)
description_en:
Public servants who interact with data on a daily basis are expected to collect and use that data in a way that is ethical and unbiased. This online self-paced course focuses on the guiding principles of data ethics, including privacy, security, and the impacts of data-driven decisions on marginalized communities. Participants will learn how data ethics can help them navigate through some of the common ethical dilemmas associated with data while maintaining unbiased and neutral data practices.

Topics include:

- understanding what data ethics is and its importance
- identifying and mitigating potential biases
- exploring the guiding principles of data ethics
- building public trust in government data management

This online self-paced course presents the fundamental concepts of data management, data quality, data privacy, data protection,
and data governance. Participants will learn about the key attributes of effective
data governance, as well as best practices for protecting data in their workplace.

Topics include:

· distinguishing between structured and unstructured data

· sequencing the stages of the data life cycle

· identifying the key attributes of data quality

· recognizing the key attributes of effective data governance

· applying best practices for protecting data in the workplace

Notes:

This course was developed with subject matter support provided by the International Institute for Analytics (www.iianalytics.com).

title_en: Analytics Literacy for Business Professionals (DDN314)
description_en:
Organizations everywhere are increasingly relying on an analytically literate workforce to support their decision-making, optimization and innovation efforts. This online self-paced course offers techniques for building strong analytics literacy in the workplace and explores the benefits of doing so. Participants will learn about common analytics pitfalls and discover best practices for supporting effective analytics practices in their organization.

Topics include:

· distinguishing between different types of analytics

· sequencing the four steps in the analytics development process

· outlining the stages in advancing the application of business analytics

· recognizing the most common mistakes when using analytics

· applying best practices for establishing and supporting an analytical organizational culture

Notes:

description_en:
Having a fundamental understanding of statistical analysis methods increases your ability to effectively apply analytics to your decision-making. This online self-paced course introduces the fundamental concepts of statistical analysis, including data distribution, deviation, correlation, regression, and clustering.
Participants will learn how to use statistical analysis methods to better communicate with data analysts and other data professionals as part of their work routine.

· recognizing the ways that deviation can be indicated

· identifying the different types of data correlation

· distinguishing between regression types

· identifying the key goals of effective clustering

title_en: Using Generative AI in the Government of Canada (DDN321)
description_en:
Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are rapidly transforming the content-creation process and offer many potential benefits to the Government of Canada. This course builds on the government’s Guide on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence by outlining key considerations when using these tools, including the importance of inclusive language and effective commands and prompts. Participants will gain the knowledge essential to navigating and applying this evolving technology through beginner-level demonstrations and applications led by specialists in the AI field.

 

Topics include:

 

·         exploring generative AI tools and identifying potential applications in the Government of Canada

·         understanding the principles of responsible use of generative AI

·         writing clear, specific and inclusive prompts to guide AI tools

·         evaluating the quality of AI-generated output

 

Notes:

 

To fully participate in this virtual, instructor-led course, participants will need their computers, as well as mobile devices with cameras capable of scanning QR codes.

 

The following resources are recommended reading for a deeper understanding of the course material:

·         Responsible use of artificial intelligence in the Government of Canada

- Guide on the use of generative artificial intelligence
title_fr: Utiliser l'IA générative au gouvernement du Canada (DDN321)
description_fr:
Les outils d’intelligence artificielle générative (IA) transforment rapidement le processus de création de contenu et pourraient présenter de nombreux avantages au gouvernement du Canada. Ce cours s’appuie sur le Guide sur l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle générative du gouvernement et souligne les principales considérations liées à l’utilisation de ces outils, dont l’importance de rédiger des requêtes efficaces et en langage inclusif. La participation au cours vise l’acquisition de connaissances essentielles pour comprendre et utiliser cette technologie en constante évolution, au moyen de démonstrations et d’applications de niveau débutant présentées par des spécialistes du domaine.

 

Sujets traités :

 

·         explorer les outils d’IA générative et déterminer ses applications possibles au gouvernement du Canada;

·         comprendre les principes d’une utilisation responsable de l’IA générative;

·         rédiger des requêtes claires, précises et en langage inclusif pour guider les outils d’IA;

·         évaluer la qualité des résultats de l’IA.

 

Remarques :

 

Pour participer pleinement à ce cours virtuel dirigé par un enseignant, il faut avoir à sa disposition son ordinateur et un appareil mobile doté d’une caméra pouvant balayer un code QR.

 

Les lectures suivantes sont recommandées pour bien comprendre le matériel du cours :

title_en: Working with Disaggregated Data for Better Policy Outcomes (DDN323)
description_en:
Disaggregated data can help policy-makers develop more targeted and effective public policies by identifying the unique needs and challenges faced by different demographic groups. This online self-paced course explains data disaggregation, how it can inform the early stages of policy development, and how it can lead to better public policy outcomes. Through videos, interactive activities and case studies, participants will learn how to identify potential target groups and guide the formulation of government initiatives.

·         understanding what disaggregated data is and why it is important

·         reflecting on the impact of disaggregated data on policy outcomes

·         extracting and synthesizing key findings, and presenting them in data tables

·         framing messages that contain disaggregated data

 

Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

title_en: Policy Implementation Case Study: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development (FON102)

• examining potential risks and mitigation strategies regarding the policy implementation process
• consulting and informing individuals impacted by policy implementation

Notes:

This course requires a time commitment of 2 hours each week for 6 weeks (12 hours total). Each week, participants will be asked to complete reading, writing or research assignments or participate in an online discussion forum.

title_en: Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Introduction (FON202)
description_en:
When developing regulatory proposals, consideration of their economic, environmental and social impacts is a critical and often mandatory first step. This course provides a general introduction to cost-benefit analysis (CBA) and demonstrates how to apply CBA to federal regulatory initiatives. Participants will become familiar with the foundational steps to completing a CBA and learn how to develop solid baseline and regulatory scenarios.


Topics include:


- understanding the analytical steps in the CBA process
- identifying costs and benefits for different stakeholder groups
- applying best practices for collaborating and meeting reporting requirements
- reviewing the information found in a CBA report


Notes:


This course is divided into two 3-hour sessions, offered on the same day of the week, one week apart, over a period of two weeks.


This course is for federal public servants at all levels who work in the regulatory field. It may also benefit those who are new to the regulatory process or to cost-benefit analysis, or anyone who has a general interest in these areas. Learners who are already familiar with the basic concepts of cost-benefit analysis are encouraged to register for Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Application (FON203) instead.

title_en: Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Application (FON203)
description_en:
Cost-benefit analysis (CBA) is a structured approach used to identify and assess potential outcomes to better inform decisions. This course explores the intricacies of the CBA process and emphasizes how rigorous analysis is pivotal to supporting evidence-based decision-making, specifically by federal regulators. Participants will acquire the skills needed to conduct a basic CBA to support the creation of a regulatory impact analysis statement (RIAS).

Topics include:

•	revisiting the theoretical foundations of CBA •	building CBA models •	assessing potential positive and negative outcomes •	supporting quantitative, qualitative and monetizing analyses •	summarizing results and drafting recommendations for decision-makers

Notes:

To receive a certificate of completion, participants must attend two virtual instructor-led sessions over the course of two weeks. They must prepare for the instructor-led sessions by also completing five online self-paced modules:


1. Self-paced modules 1 and 2
2. Virtual instructor-led session 1 (week 1; 2.5 hours)
3. Self-paced modules 3, 4 and 5
4. Virtual instructor-led session 2 (week 2; 2.5 hours)

Learners who are unfamiliar with the basic concepts of cost-benefit analysis are highly encouraged to complete Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Introduction (FON202) before registering for this course.
title_fr: Analyse coûts-avantages dans la réglementation fédérale : application (FON203)
description_fr:
L'analyse coûts-avantages est une approche structurée servant à déterminer et à évaluer d'éventuels résultats afin de prendre des décisions éclairées. Ce cours porte sur les particularités de l'analyse coûts-avantages et met l'accent sur le fait qu'une analyse rigoureuse est essentielle à la prise de décision fondée sur des données probantes, en particulier dans la réglementation fédérale. Les participants acquerront les compétences nécessaires pour faire une analyse coûts-avantages de base qui servira à l'élaboration d'un résumé de l'étude d'impact de la réglementation.

Sujets traités :

•	revoir les notions de base de l'analyse coûts-avantages; •	créer des modèles d'analyse coûts-avantages; •	évaluer les résultats éventuellement négatifs et positifs d'un règlement; •	réaliser des analyses quantitatives, qualitatives et monétaires; •	résumer des résultats et rédiger des recommandations à l'intention des décideurs.

Remarques :

Pour obtenir un certificat d’achèvement, les participants doivent assister à deux séances virtuelles dirigées par un enseignant sur une période de deux semaines. Ils doivent par ailleurs se préparer aux séances virtuelles en suivant les cinq modules à rythme libre, selon l’ordre suivant :


1. Modules 1 et 2 à rythme libre
2. Séance 1 en salle de classe virtuelle dirigée par un enseignant (semaine 1; 2,5 heures)
3. Modules 3, 4 et 5 à rythme libre
4. Séance 2 en salle de classe virtuelle dirigée par un enseignant (semaine 2; 2,5 heures)

Les personnes qui ne connaissent pas les notions de base de l'analyse coûts-avantages sont fortement encouragées à suivre le cours Analyse coûts-avantages dans la réglementation fédérale : introduction (FON202) avant de s'inscrire à ce cours-ci.

title_en: Values and Ethics Foundations for Employees (FON301)
description_en:
As part of their orientation to the public service, it is essential that all employees learn about the core values and expected behaviours shared by public servants across Canada. This online self-paced course introduces the foundational public sector values and ethical behaviours presented in the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector. Through informative exercises and scenarios, participants will learn how to identify values and ethics principles and how to integrate them into their work routines and practices.


Topics include:

·       understanding the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector

·       identifying and applying values and ethics principles

·       recognizing conflict of interest, ethical dilemmas and accountability issues

 

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for employees of the core public administration.
title_fr: Fondements des valeurs et de l'éthique pour les employés (FON301)
description_fr:
Dans le cadre de leur orientation à la fonction publique, les personnes employées doivent apprendre ce que sont les valeurs fondamentales du secteur public et les comportements attendus d'elles. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente les valeurs fondamentales et les comportements éthiques présentés dans le Code de valeurs et d'éthique du secteur public. Au moyen d'exercices et de mises en situation instructifs, les participants apprendront à reconnaître les valeurs et les principes éthiques, ainsi qu'à les intégrer à leur quotidien et à leurs pratiques de travail.


Sujets traités :

·       comprendre le Code de valeurs et d'éthique du secteur public;

·       cerner et appliquer les principes liés aux valeurs et à l'éthique;

·       reconnaître les conflits d'intérêts, les dilemmes éthiques et les responsabilités.

 

Notes :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les employées de l’administration publique centrale.

title_en: Values and Ethics Foundations for Managers (FON302)
description_en:
Public service managers have an obligation to apply the core values of the public sector in their decisions, behaviours and work environments. This online self-paced course helps managers to better understand the foundational concept of values and ethics, and how to apply it when dealing with conflicts of interest, ethical dilemmas, harassment situations and other issues of workplace well-being. Through practical exercises and case studies, participants will identify, discuss and apply the key principles and policies related to values and ethics in the public sector.   


Topics include:

·       identifying values and ethics policies and legislation

·       reviewing policies concerning post-employment measures

·       applying values and ethics to work situations and practices

 

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.
