title_en: Canada Labour Code, Part II: An Overview (WMT110)
description_en:
Part II of the Canada Labour Code protects the health and safety of employees in the federal jurisdiction. This online self-paced course provides an overview of the basic requirements and application of the Canada Labour Code for employees, supervisors and managers. Through knowledge reflection exercises, participants will be able to familiarize themselves with their respective rights, duties and responsibilities in the federal workplace.

Topics include:

·      explaining the rights and duties of employees and employers (managers and supervisors)
·      explaining the responsibilities of workplace health and safety committees and representatives
·      outlining the consequences of non-compliance and non-enforcement
·      resolving complaints and work refusals
·      outlining the requirements related to workplace inspections and hazardous occurrence investigations

Notes:
To obtain a certification of completion, participants must complete the course and attain a passing mark of 80% on the final quiz.

title_en: Mental Health and the Workplace: Raising Awareness (WMT203)
description_en:
Mental health is an essential component of our overall well-being.
This online self-paced course serves to raise awareness about the complex topic of mental health and the workplace, common signs and symptoms of potential mental health issues, and various coping and support strategies. Participants will acquire new tools and resources to support their own mental health and the well-being of their colleagues and peers.

Topics include:

• describing mental health and the relationship between mental health and the workplace

• recalling common signs and symptoms of mental health issues

• understanding how to become better aware of the state of your mental health

• identifying the principles related to supporting a culture of mental health and well-being

• accessing resources and information for mental health support

Notes:

It is not possible for this course to reflect all lived experiences. However, it does attempt to cover a range of experiences that will prompt reflection, learning, and positive action beyond the course.

title_en: Taking Stock of Your Work/Life Balance (WMT214)
description_en:
Finding the right work/life balance is beneficial not only for you, but also for your family, friends and co-workers. This online self-paced course highlights techniques for assessing balance between work and personal responsibilities, and identifies common obstacles to achieving the right balance. Participants will learn how to recognize where they are, in relation to where they want to be, as a first step in constructing a roadmap to a more balanced lifestyle.

Topics include:

• recognizing common symptoms of an out-of-balance life
• reviewing the benefits of achieving a healthy work/life balance
• assessing your work/life balance
• balancing the demands of work and private life
• overcoming internal and external obstacles

title_en: Duty to Accommodate for Managers (WMT218)
description_en:
Managers in the federal public service need a clear understanding of the considerations involved in assessing and responding to accommodation requests. This online self-paced course reviews the duty to accommodate, along with the key policies and directives that guide accommodation in the core public administration. Participants will learn about the roles and responsibilities of managers and the five-step process for evaluating and responding to workplace accommodation needs.

Topics include:

- understanding the 13 prohibited grounds of discrimination
- responding to accommodation requests in a respectful, timely and informed manner
- describing the roles of managers, employees and HR in the accommodation process
- exploring practical scenarios and best practices for evaluating accommodations

Notes:

This course provides an overview of accommodation requirements and does not replace consultation with departmental specialists in human resources, labour relations, occupational health and safety, or accessibility.
